chapters.title: Chapter 1851: I do not see how that is my problem.
paragraphs: "I AM NOT DEAD YET!!"
"Well, you are now."
With a casual look on her face, Aeliana appeared behind the no-named enemy Leader and beheaded him.
Thud
His body fell on the ground with a ’thud’. It didn’t take long for the rest of the Primordials to fall as one.
Thud Thud Thud𝗳𝚛𝗲𝕖𝕨𝕖𝗯𝚗𝚘𝕧𝕖𝗹.𝗰𝗼𝕞
One by one, their bodies fell on the ground as well, and...
Silence.
Absolute silence fell over the place.
The Soldiers and the Leaders from both Worlds stared at Aeliana, their gazes filled with awe and terror.
This woman…
She took down 17 Primordial Level Beings… all on her own…
And she made it look so easy…
Aeliana hovered in the air like a Goddess, the blood hovering with her, as if ready to follow her command.
Right now, this woman could declare the fate of 2 million lives with just a mere thought. That possibility horrified the two Worlds’ Leaders, all five of them wondering what was about to happen.
After all, one thing was already clear—they were no match for her. Even after facing 17 Primordials, there was not even a single drop of sweat on her captivating face.
It was as if… she just sprayed over a bunch of bugs that were annoying her, dealing with them in one go.
It was then...
The woman’s crimson eyes finally stared at the five Leaders.
The Leaders’ bodies flinched. The fear had rooted deep into their entire being. Unconsciously, they all lowered their heads, as if submitting to the woman.
Aeliana was used to that look; she very well knew what it meant.
"So what am I supposed to do with you now, hmm?"
She questioned lightly, none of the Leaders, however, dared to answer her.
"You three are from Velcria?"
Aeliana suddenly questioned as she stared at the three Velcrian Leaders.
"Y-Yes! We are from Velcria!"

The Velcrian Leaders nodded. They almost saluted the woman in front of them. From the very beginning, these beings had never once bowed or acted subservient to anyone. Even when their Faction sent representatives, those representatives were mostly Sovereigns or Primordials. And while they were still respectful when dealing with them, their relationship was more on an equal side.
These Leaders didn’t even know how to act subservient. Right now, however, their bodies were acting on their own, submitting to the power above them.
"Hmm."
Aeliana nodded.
Then, she glanced at the fallen Primordials and...
"You know what you are supposed to do, correct?"
She questioned, and the Velcrian Leaders trembled. They wanted their answer to satisfy this woman. A mistake could mean anything here, and they wanted to avoid the worst-case scenario by any means.
Both Kaelgran and Elaris turned towards Liora. In the end, the Seraphyte had no choice but to step forward despite her entire body screaming against it.
What else could she even do? Discuss who was going to answer and keep this woman waiting?
That was certain death!
"I-If the Lady wants, w-we will report them t-to our Faction. They have broken the Sacred Rules; they need to be held acc—"
"Don’t be foolish."
Aeliana, however, cut her off, making the Seraphyte’s body flinch again.
"If you report it to your Faction, what do you think would happen to you?"
At her question, Liora frowned.
"Do you think the enemy Faction would let you go by directing the Supreme Worlds’ wrath on them?"
Liora’s expression changed as she realized the answer to this question.
They would be annihilated from the face of the Universe without being able to show any form of resistance.
"T-Then what am I supposed to do?"
She asked as politely as she could, making sure that her question didn’t offend this woman in any way.
To her, the Faction War or whatever didn’t matter. She just wanted to live and her people to thrive.
She wanted a way out.
A way out for her and her people.
"Report it to the Enemy Faction."
Aeliana answered.
An answer that made the Velcrian and even the Trandis’s Leaders frown in confusion.
"Let the enemy Faction handle the problems within their Faction. Play no part in it, act ignorant. That is the only way you will survive."
"I-I understand. I will follow your advice."
Liora bowed her head.
Aeliana commanded, but just as she was about to leave...
"B-But Lady…"
Suddenly, another being called out.
It was Malcharon, the enemy Nightveil Leader.
Aeliana turned towards him, but despite his body flinching in fear...
"I-If they do that, our World will be destroyed."
He stuttered.
Even a child could tell how the Faction would ’handle’ problems within the Faction. Both Worlds responsible would be destroyed until there was nothing left.
Even if Tandris had nothing to do with this, even if they were in a position where they couldn’t go against the command of a Middle Level World, the Faction wouldn’t care.
To them, there was only a single solution to this problem, and Malchoron wanted to avoid that at any cost.
Just like any World Leader, he wanted to protect his own world.
Heck, from the very beginning, he and his people had only been trying to survive! It was Velcria that continuously waged war, trying to destroy their home.
However...
"And?"
Aeliana didn’t care.
"I do not see how that is my problem."
The Vampire declared coldly, and Malchoron’s body trembled.
But what could he do?
Face this woman?
He knew that even if he burned his Life Force, he would never be a match for her.
The only thing he could do was helplessly watch as he and his people got annihilated for the mistake they didn’t even make.
Aeliana stared at this man in silence.
Even if she wanted to help him, there was nothing she could do.

There were too many eyes here. Even if she didn’t make a decision here, with so many eyes, it was only a matter of time before any of the two Factions learned about what transpired here, and once they did...
It would be the end for not just one, but both worlds.
Honestly, her suggestion was the only way out for these people. The only way to save whatever lives could be saved.
"What if… we surrender?"
Suddenly, Malcharon questioned as he stared at Aeliana with a determined look on his face.
"Huh…?"

chapters.title: Chapter 1852: You can have him back
paragraphs: "What if… we surrender?"
Malcharon questioned as he stared at Aeliana with a determined look on his face.
Malcharon wasn’t a fool. What Aeliana was thinking, he understood as well. With so many eyes, the destruction of Tandris was inevitable.

Even if this woman didn’t do anything and left right now, extremists in Velcria would definitely try to get rid of their arch-nemesis. There was no way they would leave an opportunity where they could get what they wanted without having to even lift their fingers.
"Huh…?"
Aeliana narrowed her eyes.
The Nightveil continued.
"I do not know which force or faction you belong to, or even if you are truly what you claim you are, mercenaries.
What if we swear to surrender, to pledge our lives to you?
We will be your faithful servants, ready to be used as you please.
As war resources, soldiers, laborers, anything you say, we will do."
The Nightveil then suddenly knelt on the ground and,
"Please take us in."
He spoke. Read exclusive adventures at freewebnovel

Inferath, the Infernik, blinked his eyes in confusion, surprised by his comrade’s actions. But suddenly, Malcharon grabbed his arm and pulled him down so quickly that the Infernik fell to the ground, face first.
He glared at the Nightveil, only to see the latter glaring back at him. Understanding what that glare meant, he quickly collected himself, knelt down, and bowed his head.
"Please take us in."
And as if on cue.
""Please take us in.""
The Tandris soldiers who were still conscious all knelt down and bowed their heads in front of the Vampire hovering above them.
The Vampire was taken aback.
She didn’t expect this. Soon, however, she understood. These people wanted to survive and would do anything for it.
Aeliana, however, couldn’t help them. But before she could shake her head,
"Now this is an interesting development."
A voice was heard, and suddenly, the shadow of an unconscious soldier trembled and two beings materialized from it.
One, someone nobody here knew, while the other… well, someone everyone knew.
"Kaelith!"

Inferath shouted as he stared at his ally, whose body was battered up. His limbs were all bent unnaturally, his once scary crimson eyes now flickered, barely grasping life, and the dreadful aura around him that filled all his enemies with dread was nowhere to be found.
With that unknown man holding Kaelith by his neck as if he were some sort of bag, the Dreadborn looked pitiful.𝐟𝕣𝕖𝐞𝐰𝕖𝚋𝐧𝗼𝚟𝐞𝕝.𝗰𝐨𝐦
"Oh?"
The unknown man seemed to realize that he was holding one of this world’s leaders, so…
"Right, this one was roaming around in a place he shouldn’t be. Had to capture him.
No hard feelings though.
Here, you can have him back."
Nux threw the Dreadborn back to his allies.
Seeing his condition and the unknown man’s attitude, Inferath’s anger rose. However, before he could say anything, the unknown man flew in the air and moved towards that truly dreadful woman.
Then, every being standing in this place widened their eyes in disbelief as suddenly, the unknown man pulled the woman into his embrace and, with a smile on his face,
"You were a little too alluring when you were killing all of them. You are making it hard for me to control myself, Aeliana Ruinous."
What surprised everyone even further was the fact that instead of piercing this man’s body with all those weapons around her, that dreadful woman smiled back.
"You are doing this on purpose, aren’t you?"
Nux questioned, pulling Aeliana even closer to him.
"Who knows? Why don’t you try and figure it out?"
She replied in a playful tone, and Nux was barely resisting the urge to grab this woman and plunge his teeth into her neck before he burned all her clot-
Ahem.
Anyways,
As Nux controlled his desires, he finally glanced at Tandris’s leaders and,
"Some soldiers might come in handy in the future, no?"
He spoke out loud, and while his words lit up a ray of hope in the eyes of Tandris’s leaders and soldiers,
Inferath suddenly frowned.
"Wait, that man…
Tandris’s Wil-"
"Don’t open your mouth foolishly, Infernik."
Before he could complete, Nux interrupted, his eyes staring at the Infernik coldly.
"I am not as patient or forgiving as my future wife."
’Future wife…?’
Everyone who heard Nux’s words widened their eyes. However, the ’future wife’ part wasn’t the one they were reacting to.
That was only Aeliana, who was trying to hide her smile but was failing miserably.
These people were reacting to the word ’forgiving.’
’Forgiving…? Her…?’
Just staring at the butchered bodies of the Primordials made them shiver in horror.
"Inferath, shut your mouth."
On the other hand, Malcharon, who got the meaning behind Nux’s words, ordered his comrade. Inferath nodded. He understood what Nux wanted as well.
This was regarding their survival. They weren’t planning to do something foolish to mess it up.
"You plan on taking them in?"
Aeliana questioned.
"What do you think?"
Nux questioned back.
Aeliana stared at the Tandris natives who were still kneeling in front of her.
"They would be useful."
She nodded, but then, a frown appeared on her face.

"But where do you plan to keep them? Tandris will be destroyed. Their cultivation bridge would shatter. Only Sovereigns and above would survive unless we find another world for them and connect them to it."
"Finding another world, huh…
Hmm, that’s too much work..."
Nux shook his head.
If they had a free world, he would have devoured it already. Not to mention this wasn’t the first time they had seen ’pitiful people’ who had lost everything due to war, neither would it be the last.
This was the fate of the weak.
If Nux tried to protect every world he went to, it would simply become impossible, and he would be tied down with too much responsibility.
Not to mention Nux was never the Hero.
He was just a normal man who wanted to live with his wives for eternity.
These people…
He never cared about them in the first place.
"Alright, fuck it. Too much wo-"
"Take the three of us and the Sovereigns."
Before Nux could pass the ’judgment,’ Malcharon spoke up.
"What…?" Nux narrowed his eyes.
"The three Primordials and three hundred thousand Sovereigns, just take us in. Abandon the rest."

chapters.title: Chapter 1853: Do not resist.
paragraphs: "Take the three of us and the Sovereigns."
"What…?"
"The three Primordials and three hundred thousand Sovereigns, just take us in. Abandon the rest.

We will be able to survive even if our world is destroyed, and I believe that with our strength, we will not be a burden to you either. You can use us as expendables if you like. You have nothing to lose."
Malcharon spoke, and Nux raised his eyebrow.
"And then what about your people? What do you think would happen to them if you abandon them like this?"
He questioned.
"They will die."
Malcharon’s reply was quick, as if he had already considered everything.
"And you will just… let them?"
Nux tilted his head.
"I have no other choice. It doesn’t matter if I stay with them or not, they will die either way. I can only protect those I can protect."
Nux turned silent at those words.
Yes, those words were logical. With an entire faction coming after them, a low-level world like them had zero chance to survive. One or even hundreds of Primordials wouldn’t be able to do anything.
But…
"What about your family? What about your soldiers’ families? Are you going to abandon them all?"
Nux couldn’t help but question.
And he wasn’t the only one who had this question. The rest of Tandris’ soldiers were all staring at their leader with shocked looks on their faces, even the other two leaders were the same.
Malcharon could see that as well. He, however, didn’t care about anyone else and simply stared back at Nux, his words as cold as before,
"If they care about their families, they can stay back here and try to protect them. I am not forcing anyone to follow me."

The soldiers’ expressions changed when they heard those words. They exchanged uneasy glances, their loyalty to their leader wavering as they heard his words. Yet, none dared to speak and kept their heads down.
"Malcha-"
Inferath even tried to silence him, wanting him to mind his words. Malcharon, however, didn’t move his gaze away from Nux and, like an emotionless soldier, he continued,
"I suppose you would want an army that efficiently does what you tell them to, not a bunch of children dwelling in their sorrows because things didn’t go their way.
The universe is a cruel place to be in. Death can come to anyone at any time. I wish to avoid that and survive, and to do that, I will do anything I can."
"Why me?"
Nux questioned.

"Although you are weak, there are still many worlds that would be glad to accept a Primordial like you. You can even work as a mercenary, and you would do quite well. Why choose me over all that and give away your freedom?"
This time, Malcharon remained silent for a few seconds. Then, he glanced at his soldiers, who were still looking at him with disbelief, and then,
"There might be places that will be willing to accept me, but not all of them would take three hundred thousand Sovereigns together with me. If possible, I would like to remain together with them."
A burden of the leader.𝒇𝓻𝓮𝓮𝙬𝙚𝒃𝒏𝓸𝙫𝒆𝙡.𝓬𝓸𝒎
Malcharon was forced to sacrifice his people to ensure that some of his people lived. This was the best-case scenario. There were only so many he could protect, especially after they had lost.
And to make such heavy decisions with a straight face, not reflecting his emotions…
The soldiers were now able to understand their leader’s thoughts. But then,
"Bullshit."
Nux grinned, his golden eyes shining as he stared at the Nightveil standing in front of him.

"You chose me because you know the faction or the middle-level world above you will come and find you people, especially that middle-level world. Once they find out what happened here, even when they are on the verge of destruction, they would use the last of their manpower to find and kill you people.
Because of that threat, no other force would ever take you in. As for the forces who are strong enough to not worry about such matters, you simply have no use for them.
You have no other choice but me."
Nux’s grin widened even further as he said the next words.
"You lied to me."
Malcharon was silent, his face didn’t reflect any emotion.
Suddenly, Nux flew towards Malcharon and the other two Tandris leaders. Their bodies flinched, especially Kaelith’s.
Step Step Step
Nux slowly walked towards them. The leaders remained on their knees, and as Nux stared into their eyes, he questioned again,
"So you wish to serve me?"
Nux questioned.
"Yes."
Malcharon nodded, and the other two nodded.
"I have a few rules."

A Sovereign threatening to kill them, Primordials?
How laughable!
The only reason this boy was still alive was because of that woman hovering behind him.
’Tsk.’
In the end, Inferath could only snort in his head.
"Now the second rule,"
Nux continued, completely ignoring the Primordials’ expressions.
Whoosh Whoosh Whoosh
Suddenly, a few portals appeared in the air, and nine women walked out of them. They were the mercenaries these people had seen before.
"Treat them as you would treat your Goddesses,"
Nux’s words were heard, then he glanced at Kaelith with an expression that would terrify even the fiercest demons, and then,
"Disrespect them,"
Nux extended his arm, pointing toward Kaelith, and suddenly, Kaelith’s body started hovering in the air.
"And this is what is going to happen to you."

Suddenly, the ’Seed’ in Kaelith’s body reacted. His entire body was quickly surrounded by cold black energy. He tried to resist, wanting to eject this strange energy out of his body, but no matter what he did, his own energy, despite being of a higher quality than Nux’s, couldn’t do anything against it.
It was as if he had no control inside his own body.
The dark energy continued to increase, engulfing every part of his body from the inside. Panic surged in. Kaelith started moving frantically, but he was helpless.
He couldn’t do anything.

Neither could he access his own energy anymore, nor could he move like he wished to. He seemed like a bug frantically moving its limbs in desperation while it was hanged in the air using an invisible string.
Then, something even scarier happened.
The black energy that had engulfed his entire body started draining his life force.
"AAGGGHHHH!! NO, NO!
I DO NOT WISH TO DIE!!!
PLEASE FORGIVE ME!!!"
The Dreadborn screamed in terror, begging for his life. Nux, however, simply glanced at Inferath, making his body flinch, before he turned toward the Tandris Soldiers and said,
"Etch this sight in your minds.
It doesn’t matter who you are, how much contribution you have made, what backings you have, or how strong you are,
The day you disrespect them or break any other rules I set,
This will be your end."
"AAGGGGHHHH!!!"
As Nux’s words ended, so did the Dreadborn’s screams.
Thud

"Take command of the army. Sort them out."

"Yes, my Lord."

He actually did it…
A Sovereign killed a Primordial…
What sort of monstrosity were they dealing with…?
And… why does no one around this man seem surprised…?
Of course, Inferath didn’t dare to ask any of these questions. He simply walked behind his comrade, who, lord knows how, was still calm in his situation.
Malcharon stared at his soldiers. The soldiers were full of uncertainty, doubt, and… fear.
Malcharon stared at them for a few seconds, then he flew into the air. Inferath followed, and the soldiers glanced at their leaders.
"Those who do not wish to follow me and serve our savior, stand up while the others keep kneeling."
His words were clear.
Once again, the soldiers exchanged uneasy glances. They had countless questions in their minds.
What would happen to them?
What about their families?
What were they supposed to do?
Malcharon, however, seemed to have no intention of answering those questions.
Honestly, most soldiers who could understand their situation had already made a decision. A few, however, still couldn’t abandon their families, so they decided to stand up.
One after another, more and more soldiers stood up, and once Malcharon confirmed no one else would follow, he stared at the soldiers who did stand and questioned, Experience new tales on freewebnovel
"I assume you wish to die together with your families?"
"Yes, we wish to try and protect everyone we can…"
One of the soldiers nodded. The rest nodded as well.
By now, Nux wasn’t very interested in them. He and his women, together with Aeliana, had gathered at one point, and suddenly,
"Are you sure about this?"
Ember questioned.
It was a question everyone else had in their minds.
"If you take them in, it will not be surprising if both factions come after you."
"It is definitely a possibility."
Nux nodded with a light smile on his face as he walked in a particular direction.

"But do you think a faction would waste its resources to find a bunch of Primordials? The biggest concern here was that the rules set by the Supreme Worlds were broken. The two worlds that did that will be destroyed, ensuring the Supreme Worlds’ dominance and their ’face.’
No one would care about this matter anymore than that."
Nux shrugged.
Aeliana, however, shook her head.
"Not many would, but that Middle Level World would. They would send people to find out who we are, and since they know quite a lot of Primordials have died…"
The Vampire stared at Nux and continued,
"They might send a Transcendent this time."
Nux paused. He turned around and glanced at his future wife.
"Yes, that is possible as well."
He accepted, then he retrieved a black sword from a corpse—a sword that Aeliana recognized in an instant—and Nux continued,
"But now we might not be as helpless against a Transcendent as we think, no?"
Nux spoke, and Aeliana widened her eyes in disbelief.
The enemy leader’s Relic…
A weapon capable of killing even a Transcendent.
"Nux, you…"

paragraphs: "Nux, you…"
Aeliana called out, however, before she could say anything, Nux’s eyes fell on the Velcrian Leaders.
The three leaders flinched, Nux’s gaze lingered on Kaelgran for a little longer, making the stone dude sweat buckets.
His race didn’t even sweat in the first place!
"What are you standing there for? Scram."
Nux ordered with a cold look on his face and in an instant, the Leaders reacted.

Liora actually wanted to talk to Ember, however, seeing the latter had no interest in the conversation, not to mention that man’s intimidating gaze that stared at them like a predator who would pounce on them at any moment, the Seraphyte decided not to bother Ember and together with her comrades, she flew in the air.
With a wave of her hand, the unconscious Velcrian soldiers’ bodies rose in the air, the Sovereigns who were still conscious, flew as well, almost all of them staring at the man and their General.
"We are thankful for what you have done, General Ember and her party."
Liora bowed her head before placing the soldiers in the battle fleets and leaving Tandris.
’Lane?’
After they left, Nux called out using his Universe’s connection.
’I am in their fleet.’
Lane answered and Nux nodded. He had sent Lane to keep an eye on the Velcrians just to be safe.
’Be safe.’
’Don’t worry, if something happens, I will die.’
Lane replied and Nux just stared in a random direction with a blank look on his face.
’Why do I feel like you are being influenced by Shadow?’
He questioned with a frown here.
’How was I brought up here?’
Shadow complained.
Everyone turned silent and noticing this, Shadow frowned.
’Why do I feel like you guys are ignoring me?’
’Hey? Hey! Lane! You out of all people should be on my side, no? I am you!’
’Lies.’
Lane defended herself.
’Oh come on! You are just lying to yourself. Just accept your true self, come to the dark side~
We hav-’
’Shut up.’
Lane snorted before she stopped replying altogether.
’Nux, I am sad.’
Shadow complained with a pout.
’I am here, what do you want?’
Nux questioned gently, his voice full of warmth and love, completely opposite to how he was with everyone here in Tandris.
The Tandris soldiers might even puke in disgust and indignance if they heard Nux speak such words in this manner.𝐟𝚛𝕖𝚎𝕨𝗲𝐛𝚗𝐨𝐯𝐞𝕝.𝐜𝗼𝗺
’Fuck me.’
Shadow requested and before Nux could reply—
’Don’t you dare, you bitch.
It is my turn next.’
Amaya jumped in.
’Weren’t you cultivating!? Where did you come from?’
Shadow retorted.
’I always have my eyes on you.’
’Fuck you! I don’t swing that way.’
Even Amaya had a difficult time dealing with Shadow.
Nux, who saw his women act like this, just chuckled inwardly.
On the other hand, Aeliana, who was waiting till all the Tandris soldiers left, glanced at Nux again and,
"Nux, that sword…"
"Mhm, the Relic."
Read exclusive adventures at freewebnovel
Nux nodded.
"That sword is capable of hurting even the Transcendents?"
"That is correct. We can even kill one if we have this."
"We can kill one?"
Aeliana couldn’t believe what she was hearing.
"Do not underestimate the Relics, Aeliana.

These are the creations of the Supreme World of Eternity, a world that is strong enough to face other Supreme Worlds despite having to depend on the rest of the Universe. The reason behind this is because they have these Relics."
After absorbing Umbrasol, Nux’s knowledge about the Universe had risen quite a lot. From Umbrasol’s perspective, he had seen how the Eternity’s Relics affected things on the grand scale of things.
Even their weakest Relics, like this sword, were priceless.
Offer someone a choice between a Low-Level World or a Relic, and 90% would choose the Relic, even if it is the weakest of the bunch.
This was simply how important these things were.

This was also the reason Nux was so surprised when he saw a Primordial wielding a Relic like this. Nux was positive that this man was someone with extreme influence back in his own world. He wouldn’t be surprised if he was a direct descendant of one of the World Leaders.
Nux also knew that just because this Relic was now in his hand, that Middle-Level World would never leave him alone.
Not that it mattered, after all, if he wanted to run away, not even the Supreme World could catch him, let alone a mere Middle-Level World.
"The Relics of the Supreme World of Eternity, huh…"
Thyra muttered silently.
"Of course, this is still an extremely weakened version of the weapons they have, but to deal with a Transcendent, these are more than enough."
Nux nodded.
"So… you are saying you are now capable of killing a Transcendent?"
Aeliana questioned.
Just seeing a Sovereign facing and defeating Primordials was already absurd…
But to think now this man could…
"Of course not."
Nux shook his head and for some reason, the women around him… sighed in relief?
Yes, they wanted Nux to be the strongest, they wanted him to be the best, but…
They still wanted to be able to make some sense of all this! The sight of a Sovereign killing a Transcendent would simply break them if they were not already broken!
Even absurdity has its own limit.
"Transcendents are strong."
Nux accepted and the women around him nodded continuously, agreeing with his words.
"Even if a Relic allows one to ignore the ’quality’ of one’s energy since it replaces the being’s energy with its own, to activate it, one still requires an absurd amount of energy.
To kill a Transcendent, you would need Transcendent-level energy.
You are technically trying to replace your own energy with that of Transcendent-level energy, of course, the quantity of the energy you use in the process will be absurd."
Nux explained and Ember nodded, making it simpler.
"So you are replacing quality with quantity, and in theory, it would never be enough."
"Mhm, most would run out of energy within a few minutes. Even that Primordial couldn’t use this Relic at its full strength for more than five minutes."
Nux, however, glanced at Aeliana with a grim look on his face and,
"But in those five minutes he had, if his attack connected with you even once, you would not survive."
Aeliana turned silent and her face turned grim.
"Wait…"
Suddenly, Astaria called out as she glanced at Nux.
"If all this… Relic needs is energy…
Do you not have an almost infinite amount of it?
Does that mean you can use this Relic at its full capacity for as long as you want?"
"Mm?"
Nux glanced at Astaria and at her question,
"Ah, yes.
That is correct."
He nodded casually.

Amaya jumped in.
’Weren’t you cultivating!?
Where did you come from?’
Shadow retorted.
’I always have my eyes on you.’
’Fuck you!
I don’t swing that way.’
Even Amaya had a difficult time dealing with Shadow.
Nux, who saw his women act like this, just chuckled inwardly.
On the other hand, Aeliana, who was waiting till all the Tandris soldiers left, glanced at Nux again and,
"Nux, that sword…"
"Mhm, the Relic."
Read exclusive adventures at freewebnovel
Nux nodded.
"That sword is capable of hurting even the Transcendents?"
"That is correct.
We can even kill one if we have this."
"We can kill one?"
Aeliana couldn’t believe what she was hearing.
"Do not underestimate the Relics, Aeliana.
These are the creations of the Supreme World of Eternity, a world that is strong enough to face other Supreme Worlds despite having to depend on the rest of the Universe.
The reason behind this is because they have these Relics."
After absorbing Umbrasol, Nux’s knowledge about the Universe had risen quite a lot.
From Umbrasol’s perspective, he had seen how the Eternity’s Relics affected things on the grand scale of things.
Even their weakest Relics, like this sword, were priceless.
Offer someone a choice between a Low-Level World or a Relic, and 90% would choose the Relic, even if it is the weakest of the bunch.
This was simply how important these things were.
This was also the reason Nux was so surprised when he saw a Primordial wielding a Relic like this.
Nux was positive that this man was someone with extreme influence back in his own world.
He wouldn’t be surprised if he was a direct descendant of one of the World Leaders.
Nux also knew that just because this Relic was now in his hand, that Middle-Level World would never leave him alone.
Not that it mattered, after all, if he wanted to run away, not even the Supreme World could catch him, let alone a mere Middle-Level World.
"The Relics of the Supreme World of Eternity, huh…"
Thyra muttered silently.
"Of course, this is still an extremely weakened version of the weapons they have, but to deal with a Transcendent, these are more than enough."
Nux nodded.
"So… you are saying you are now capable of killing a Transcendent?"
Aeliana questioned.
Just seeing a Sovereign facing and defeating Primordials was already absurd…
But to think now this man could…
"Of course not."
Nux shook his head and for some reason, the women around him… sighed in relief?
Yes, they wanted Nux to be the strongest, they wanted him to be the best, but…
They still wanted to be able to make some sense of all this!
The sight of a Sovereign killing a Transcendent would simply break them if they were not already broken!
Even absurdity has its own limit.
"Transcendents are strong."
Nux accepted and the women around him nodded continuously, agreeing with his words.
"Even if a Relic allows one to ignore the ’quality’ of one’s energy since it replaces the being’s energy with its own, to activate it, one still requires an absurd amount of energy.
To kill a Transcendent, you would need Transcendent-level energy.
You are technically trying to replace your own energy with that of Transcendent-level energy, of course, the quantity of the energy you use in the process will be absurd."
Nux explained and Ember nodded, making it simpler.
"So you are replacing quality with quantity, and in theory, it would never be enough."
"Mhm, most would run out of energy within a few minutes.
Even that Primordial couldn’t use this Relic at its full strength for more than five minutes."
Nux, however, glanced at Aeliana with a grim look on his face and,
"But in those five minutes he had, if his attack connected with you even once, you would not survive."
Aeliana turned silent and her face turned grim.
"Wait…"
Suddenly, Astaria called out as she glanced at Nux.
"If all this…
Relic needs is energy…
Do you not have an almost infinite amount of it?
Does that mean you can use this Relic at its full capacity for as long as you want?"
"Mm?"
Nux glanced at Astaria and at her question,
"Ah, yes.
That is correct."
He nodded casually.

chapters.title: Chapter 1856: You are irreplaceable.
paragraphs: "Wait,
If all this… Relic needs is energy…
Do you not have almost an infinite amount of it?
Does that mean you can use this Relic at its full capacity for as long as you want?"
Astaria questioned.
"Mm?"
Nux glanced at the Swordswoman and, at her question,
"Ah, yes.
That is correct."
He nodded.
Nux’s energy reserves were high from the beginning since he constantly devoured his own cultivation and reached a saturation point.
However, after Astral Bond, the ability that allows him to ’borrow’ the power from the Worlds inside him, his energy reserves were simply endless, higher than even that of a Transcendent.
"So you just got a weapon capable of killing a Transcendent and you can use it without any limitations whatsoever?"
Astaria questioned directly.
"Yes, pretty much."
"So you are capable of killing Transcendents?"
"No."
Nux shook his head again.
"If I want to kill a Transcendent, that Transcendent would need to stand still, allowing me to behead him without showing any resistance whatsoever."
Nux stared at Aeliana and continued,
"You should know.
Yes, the biggest difference between cultivators of two phases is the quality of their energy, however, this doesn’t mean that is all there is to it.

A Transcendent is much faster and stronger than me, a Transcendent can create a Domain where their Law is Absolute, their reaction speed and ability to judge the situation is also at an entirely different level,
So even if we use Relics to undermine the difference in the quality of energy, can I defeat a Transcendent?
That is not possible.

If the enemy is one of the weakest Transcendents who relies on strength and is on the slower side, then by combining all my abilities and this Relic, I might stand a chance, but against a normal Transcendent, in a one-on-one battle,
I cannot win."
Nux shook his head, explaining his thoughts.
The women nodded in understanding.
And…
Inferath, who was eavesdropping on their conversation, couldn’t help but feel his entire world falling apart.
Were these people in their right mind!?
Find your next adventure on freewebnovel
Who in the hell asks a Sovereign whether he can defeat a Transcendent or not!?
And what is with that detailed answer as if this question was actually worth considering!? Was this bastard actually thinking of facing a Transcendent!?
Sure, he might have used some sort of extremely powerful trick to get control over their lives, but… to think of facing a Transcendent…?
Inferath could see it…
His bleak future where he would lose his life under this madman’s command.
Gulp
The Infernik gulped and accepted his fate.
He also promised himself to enjoy whatever limited life he was left with.
While Infernik was questioning his life choices and making new life goals, Melia glanced at Nux and,
"What about them? Where do we keep them?"
"I was thinking of using that Dead World as a Base."
Nux answered as he recalled the World where he killed the five Primordials who were after these women.
"There were Primordial Level Beasts there, quite a lot of them actually."
"Meh, we will deal with it."
Nux shrugged, the sword in his hand gleamed.
"Nux…"
Suddenly, Astaria called out with a frown.
"Hm?"
"What if… you use this sword at its full capacity and… face a Primordial?"
"The faster Primordials might give me a difficult time since I would have a difficult time attacking them."
Nux answered.
"And what if… they are not fast?
How many strikes do you need to get rid of them…?"
Astaria questioned carefully. Honestly, she already had an answer in her mind; she was just having a hard time believing that answer.
But…
"One."
Nux answered, and Astaria’s mouth twitched.
"So this is like my Law? A sword that can cut anything?"
She questioned.
The woman was in the middle of having a crisis.
Nux, however, glanced at Astaria, his expression solemn.
"Do not be foolish, Astaria.
You are underestimating yourself."
He looked into the swordswoman’s eyes and,
"If you, as you are now, go to the Supreme World, they would take you, no questions asked.
Why do you think that is if they can counter your Law with just some weapon?"
Astaria was silent.
"It doesn’t matter what World you come from or what level of bloodline you have, to the Universe, those things never mattered,
Laws, however, are different.
Laws are a sign that the Universe acknowledges your existence.
And Absolutes…
An Absolute Law is a sign that even the Universe acknowledges you as the strongest.
Even a High Level World like Umbrasol didn’t have more than 100 beings with Absolute Law.
These Laws cannot be passed down from generation to generation, nor can these be ’extracted’ by any methods, not even the Supreme Worlds can do that.
Yes, this sword is strong enough to kill a Primordial in one slash, but…
What if the Primordial has a defensive relic?
This is where the sword fails.
Your sword, however, as long as you are strong enough, would never fail."
Nux held his Star’s hands and,
"Astaria, your sword can cut through everything.
Even the relics.
You, my Star, are irreplaceable."
Astaria turned silent, Nux’s words echoing in her mind.
"Are my words clear?"
Nux questioned, his tone firm.
"Mm."
Astaria nodded in a low voice, then a light smile appeared on her face, and, unable to control himself, Nux sealed her lips.
Aeliana, who saw that scene, felt a strange emotion. To avoid that, she shook her head and, as if trying to divert her mind, she questioned out loud,
"What’s next? Now that the mission is complete, what do we do now?"

After all, the true goal for all this was to find information about worlds that are not connected with his wives whatsoever, are at war, and on the verge of destruction, so Nux could go there and devour them without gaining much attention from both the Universe and the Higher Level Worlds.
"Well, we need to find someone who would know what we want to know. I doubt a Low Level World would know much."
Aisha muttered.
"Someone from a Middle Level World should know."
Rune spoke.
The women, however, glanced at the butchered bodies of the possible information providers and then glanced at Aeliana.
"Right… I was supposed to capture him alive…"
Aeliana muttered as she glanced at the enemy leader.
"Well, it doesn’t matter."
Allura, however, shook her head and shrugged, and seeing the women turning towards her with a frown, she tilted her head as well, confused.
"Hmm? What? Did you forget the poor fellow who jumped into the portal ’after’ us?"
The instant she said those words, the women’s eyes widened in surprise.
They had actually forgotten about that fellow.
And the fellow who they had all forgotten about was currently in a Dead World, standing against a tall woman with dragon scales covering her body, while her golden eyes shined intensely,
"Are you prepared?"
Vyriana questioned with a wide grin as she cracked her fingers, prepared for the battle.
She had been holding back for such a long time. Now, however, when the target himself had jumped out of the portal, delivering himself to her, she could finally have her fun.
As for the poor fellow, well, he could only curse his luck.
It was probably better to die under the barrage of blood weapons.

chapters.title: Chapter 1857: Clean up
paragraphs: "Malcharon."
Nux called out as he walked towards the Nightveil. The women followed behind him.
"My Lord."
The Nightveil knelt down. Clearly, the man was desperate to show his loyalty.
Nux didn’t stop him either.
"Are you done?"
He just asked the question.
"Yes, My Lord."
Malcharon nodded.
"The people behind me have all decided to submit to me."
At his words, Nux looked behind, and his eyes fell on around 200,000 Sovereigns, all kneeling on the floor with their heads low.
Nux raised his eyebrow.
"That’s quite a number."
"Now I regret killing the rest. I would have held back if I knew this would happen."
Ember commented, and at her words, the rest of the women nodded. After all, they had killed quite a few.
Malcharon and the army stayed silent.
"What about the rest?"
Nux questioned.
"They decided to stay in Tandris.
Does the Lord want me to deal with them?"
"Oh? What are you going to do?"
Nux questioned with a curious look on his face.
"I can kill them all if the Lord feels it would be troublesome to deal with them."
Once again, at Malcharon’s words, the soldiers behind him trembled as they exchanged nervous glances.
Nux, who noticed that, couldn’t help but comment,
"You know, Malcharon,
To say such words in front of your soldiers, they won’t be very loyal to you if this continues."
"They should know that I am doing this for their own sake."
Malcharon answered, and seeing how fast he did that, Nux just stared at the soldiers behind the Nightveil, and in the end, he just shrugged.
"Oh well, not that any of this matters."
Then, Nux stepped forward and stared at his ’soldiers.’
"Are you all willing to be my slaves?"
The soldiers exchanged glances, confused.
What was this man trying to do?
Slaves?
Weren’t they being recruited?
Of course, Nux didn’t give them enough time to think this through.
"I do not like to repeat myself."
And the instant he said those words,
BOOM
The Nightveil released his Aura.
"Answer the Lord’s question."
His words echoed throughout the battlefield and in an instant,
"Yes, our Lord."

The soldiers answered in unison, and suddenly, a foreign energy entered their bodies. The soldiers frowned. They tried to use their own energy to try and understand what this energy was; some even tried to push it out of their bodies, but then,
"AAAGgGGgGGhHhhhHHHH!!!"
A few soldiers fell on the ground, screeching in pain.
"Malcharon, follow me."
Nux, completely ignoring them, ordered Malcharon and flew in the air. Malcharon followed.
"All the artifacts you have or your people have, show me."
Nux ordered.
It was time to take the spoils of war.
"Yes, my Lord."
"Start thinking about being loyal to him and the pain shall stop. Look at others around you; none of them felt such pain because none of them harbored the thought of going against him."
On the other side, Ember, together with the other women who stood in front of the army of Sovereigns, stepped forward and spoke in a calm tone.
At her words, some soldiers, who followed her advice, stopped writhing in pain. The rest, however, were still rolling on the ground, feeling pain they never thought was possible to feel.
"You are now slaves, just like you agreed to. If even a mere thought of betraying your Master enters your mind, you will feel this pain, and it will continue until that thought goes away."
Ember stared at all the soldiers and,
"So I suggest you stay loyal to your Master and not try something funny.
Trust me,
That man can do worse things."
As her words ended, all the soldiers felt a chill running down their spines. Even Inferath, who had stayed back, trembled. He had never seen his soldiers scream in such agony.
By then, Nux and Malcharon returned as well.𝙛𝒓𝓮𝙚𝔀𝒆𝒃𝓷𝒐𝓿𝙚𝓵.𝙘𝒐𝒎
"Did you find something?"
Astaria questioned.
Nux shook his head.
"Somewhat. There are around a hundred Chains of Soul, the shield they used before the battle began, and some other artifacts these people call treasures.
Nothing too impressive though; none of the artifacts would be of any use against Transcendent Level Beings."
The women stared at this man in silence.
"What about the Relic? Did you connect with it yet?"
Astaria questioned.
Relics were different from normal weapons or artifacts. Since they had consciousness, one needed to form a connection with them before being able to use them.

It wasn’t a long process. Since the Relic’s owner was dead, Nux could become its next owner. While there are some Relics who ’choose their owner on their own,’ they are much stronger than normal artifacts. The weakest Relics do not have such limitations, else that Leader would have never been able to use it in the first place.
Nux, however, had a different problem when it came to connecting with the Relic.
"The Relics come from the Supreme World of Eternity…
I do not wish to create a link that connects us with them just yet."
"Hmm? Are you saying forming a connection with a Relic forms a link with the Supreme World of Eternity?"
Aeliana tilted her head in doubt.
"I am not sure."
Nux shook his head.
Even with all the knowledge he had, the information regarding the Supreme Worlds was severely limited.

"The Umbrasol Progenitors had doubts that the Supreme Worlds were keeping an eye on them through these Relics. It would make sense, since an Infinity appeared just when they thought everything was working out.
Of course, there is a chance that I am wrong, not to mention, as we are right now, the Supreme Worlds wouldn’t even care about our existence, but for now,
Let’s keep all the gates closed and avoid troubles, okay?"
Nux spoke, and the women nodded, especially Aeliana. Your next journey awaits at freewebnovel
"Mhm, even Father wanted you to stay away from the Supreme Worlds."
"Does Lord Azriel not have a Relic of his own?"
Melia questioned with a curious look on her face. Aeliana, however, shook her head.
"If he did, he didn’t tell me about it."
Nux, however, shook his head.
"That man probably doesn’t even need one."
None of the women doubted those words.
"Anyways, what do we do now?"
"Well…"
Before Nux could say anything.
"We need to go to Velcria."
Ember spoke up.
"Hmm?"
Everyone turned towards her, and the Dragon smiled.
"We completed the mission. Don’t you think we should be rewarded?"
At those words, the rest grinned as well.

"The Relics come from the Supreme World of Eternity…
I do not wish to create a link that connects us with them just yet."
"Hmm?
Are you saying forming a connection with a Relic forms a link with the Supreme World of Eternity?"
Aeliana tilted her head in doubt.
"I am not sure."
Nux shook his head.
Even with all the knowledge he had, the information regarding the Supreme Worlds was severely limited.
"The Umbrasol Progenitors had doubts that the Supreme Worlds were keeping an eye on them through these Relics.
It would make sense, since an Infinity appeared just when they thought everything was working out.
Of course, there is a chance that I am wrong, not to mention, as we are right now, the Supreme Worlds wouldn’t even care about our existence, but for now,
Let’s keep all the gates closed and avoid troubles, okay?"
Nux spoke, and the women nodded, especially Aeliana.

"Mhm, even Father wanted you to stay away from the Supreme Worlds."
"Does Lord Azriel not have a Relic of his own?"
Melia questioned with a curious look on her face.
Aeliana, however, shook her head.
"If he did, he didn’t tell me about it."
Nux, however, shook his head.
"That man probably doesn’t even need one."
None of the women doubted those words.
"Anyways, what do we do now?"
"Well…"
Before Nux could say anything.
"We need to go to Velcria."
Ember spoke up.
"Hmm?"
Everyone turned towards her, and the Dragon smiled.
"We completed the mission.
Don’t you think we should be rewarded?"
At those words, the rest grinned as well.

chapters.title: Chapter 1858: The Dragon was angry.
paragraphs: The Velcrian Leaders stared at the 200,000-man strong army hovering in the air in front of them with nervous looks on their faces.
While the army itself didn’t really bother them, the woman standing at the very front of the army did.
A woman who massacred 17 Primordials alone…
Yes, she was with them as well.
"Liora, it has been a while."
Suddenly, Liora heard a greeting.
It was Ember.
’We parted an hour ago.’
Liora wished to say those words; she, however, didn’t dare to say them out loud.
"E-Ember, it has been a while indeed."
She smiled, playing along with the Dragon’s game.
"What brings you here?"
At her question, Ember glanced at Kaelgran. The Stoneborn’s eyes widened in disbelief as his body froze.
It was the end!
These women had finally come for him!
He knew this would happen!
The Stoneborn gulped, trying to think of a way out. Even if he had to kneel and kowtow, he was prepared.
As for trying to resist them? He wasn’t a fool. He stood no chance, even if he called forth all his allies. It would just lead to more useless deaths.
Seeing his condition, Ember chuckled.
"Things here are much different than the first time we came here."
’Well, we are here with an army now…
So that is quite obvious.’
Allura chuckled.
’I don’t think the army is what they are worried about.’
Rune replied, her eyes staring at Aeliana.
She had seen the woman fight and was wondering if she could ever defeat her, even if she became a Primordial.
"You did help us win the War, so it isn’t surprising if people see you differently now.
You are practically a goddess in their eyes."
Liora chuckled.
’She always had a way with her words,’
Aisha commented.
’Mhm.’
Thyra nodded.
’I still like the Sylvanix more; they look so cute.’
Skyla muttered.
’Anyways, Nux is waiting. Stop wasting time here.’
Astaria spoke; she had no interest in this world now.
"Yes, this is why we are here."
Ember nodded.
"You still have not rated my party’s performance and confirmed the completion of the mission yet."
Ember spoke, and with a wave of her hands, a bunch of documents flew towards Liora.
"O-Oh! Right!" Experience exclusive tales on freewebnovel𝗳𝐫𝚎𝗲𝚠𝚎𝗯𝕟𝐨𝘃𝚎𝗹.𝗰𝗼𝗺
Liora nodded, her expression brightening up the instant she heard those words. She quickly caught those documents and,
"Of course! We cannot hope for a better performance. Not only were the number of casualties merely in the thousands because of your exceptional leadership ability,"
Liora’s eyes fell on Aeliana, and,
"Your friend saved all our lives. We are eternally grateful to you."
Liora bowed her head; Elaris and Kaelgran followed.
"I have confirmed the completion of your missions, and I have also prepared the rewards."
Liora spoke.
"Yes, that is another reason we are here for."
Ember interrupted.
"100 ships."
She spoke directly, without playing any games.
"H-Hundred?"
Liora’s eyes widened in surprise.
"Hmm? Do you not think our performance deserves a bonus reward?"
Aisha chuckled at Liora’s reaction, and the Seraphyte’s face paled.
’Why do I feel like we are the bad guys here?’
Skyla commented with a slight frown on her face.
’She said it on her own. We saved their lives; don’t you think we deserve a reward for that?’
Allura answered.
’Bu-’
’Shh.
We are the good guys.’
The succubus shushed the innocent maid before she could say anything more.
"I-I understand."
In the end, Liora agreed as well.
She didn’t really have much choice, and honestly, thinking about it, Ember’s demands were extremely reasonable. In fact, she was underpaid.
Velcria didn’t even have the resources to hire a normal Primordial, let alone…
That crimson-eyed woman hovering in the air.
"I will arrange the ships. Please give me a moment."
The Seraphyte nodded as she signaled her men to move.
With almost a third of their ships gone, it would cause quite a lot of trouble, and they would probably need to ask for more from their faction, but it didn’t matter.
As long as they were alive, they could think of something.
"You, what is your name?"
On the other side, Nux, who had come to the Dead World Vyriana was in together with a Sovereign Level Dreadborn, questioned.
"Grafan."
The Dreadborn answered politely.
"Grafan, can you use Shadow Walk?"
"Yes, my Lord."
"Alright,"
Nux nodded, and then, he threw the Relic towards him.
"Connect with it."
He ordered.
"W-What?"
Grafan blinked in surprise; he knew what this was.
"Do what I said."
Nux ordered.
"Y-Yes."
Grafan quickly connected with the Relic, and Nux nodded.

His plan was simple. If he ever needed to use it, he would make Grafan break his connection and take the weapon from him. Since Grafan could use Shadow Walk, he could enter his Universe, making it possible for Nux to have the Relic with him all the time.
As for the main Universe detecting Grafan’s disappearance?
Nux had a solution for that as well.
He would take the Dreadborn to Umbrasol and, using the Veil to his advantage, take him inside his Universe.
Yes, from now on, Grafan would stay in his Universe, with his only purpose being the carrier of the sword.
Nux also considered the possibility of the Supreme World of Eternity finding out about his Universe through Grafan. Soon, however, he shook his head.

The Veil could even fool the Universe. The Supreme World should be the same. If those beings were actually keeping an eye on every Relic Holder, then for them, Grafan should be no different than all other beings who lost their lives in Umbrasol.
Nux highly doubted those beings would think too much about the weakest bunch of Relics, and if that’s not the case?
Well, then in the end,
Nux would need to prepare himself and face the Supreme Worlds.
Thinking about it, Nux shook his head, and then, he walked towards Vyriana,
Who was sitting on the poor Primordial’s unconscious body, which was full of bruises, with a bored look on her face, waiting for him.
The moment she saw him, she appeared next to him and tried to punch him. Nux, however, countered her punch in an instant and grabbed her from behind.
"Missed me?"
He whispered into her ears.
"You dare send just one of them? Why did you close the portal!?"
The Dragon was angry.

chapters.title: Chapter 1859: Doesn’t that mean Yrniel is in danger…?
paragraphs: "This is my second time seeing this, but it still seems to affect me.
It is quite a cruel method,"
Vyriana commented as she sat on Nux’s lap like a queen, as if it was her right. Nux held her from behind, caressing her body as the dragon let herself be comforted by his touch.
"Well, I am not a fan of it either. I tried to be nice,"
Nux spoke as he stared at the Primordial’s soul, which had almost a hundred pins embedded in it. The soul floated in the air, expressionless.
Just like Etheryn, he had stopped resisting and accepted his fate. Umbrasol’s Soul Torture was simply too agonizing, even when compared to the Slave Seal.
Thinking that this should be enough, Nux waved his hand, and the being’s soul went back to his half-dead body.
The body jerked, but the man showed no reaction to the change around him.
Nux didn’t care either. He simply extended his hand, and the man’s body started floating in the air before it flew toward him.
Nux grabbed the man’s head, and a few strange patterns and texts appeared all over the Primordial’s body.
It was the ability he had gained from devouring Aetherial—an ability that allowed him to absorb knowledge.
It was one of the better ways to read someone’s memories.
He had tried to do it before, but the Primordial had continued to resist his energy, and since Nux’s energy quality was lacking, he couldn’t overpower the Primordial.
Even after a total of three warnings, the Primordial didn’t listen and continued to resist Nux’s energy. In the end, Nux had no choice but to use Soul Severance.
Ten minutes later, the Primordial broke down, and now…
Now Nux felt no resistance as his energy moved into the man’s body, and he started absorbing his memories.
The entire process took five minutes, and once Nux was done, he opened his eyes and threw the Primordial’s body aside, keeping him alive.

The Universe already knew that this ’entity’ had interacted with an entity called Aeliana Ruinous. If this being died for ’no apparent reason,’ the Universe might find it odd, and its attention might fall on Aeliana Ruinous.
So Nux waited for Aeliana to come here by ship and kill him herself.
’Tsk, there are too many restrictions. I do not like it.’
Nux snorted inwardly. Explore stories at freewebnovel
Yes, he was being extremely paranoid since the Universe usually wouldn’t even care if an ’entity’ died as long as it returned to it. After all, to it, ’death’ was never the true end.
Nux, however, still played it safe.
He didn’t want to take any risks when it came to his wives… or future wife.
"Did you find anything?" Vyriana’s voice brought Nux out of his reverie.
"Mhm." Nux nodded.
"Got five of them. One Lowest Level and four Low-Level Worlds."
"Just five?" The Dragon frowned.
This man was from a Middle-Level World. A Middle-Level World managed countless Low and Lowest Level Worlds, especially during wars. Vyriana found it strange that he didn’t know more.
"Five are quite a lot."
Nux, however, had a different opinion.
"I am looking for worlds he cannot be linked to. If it is a world he, his subordinates, his friends, or even his acquaintances have visited, I need to remove it from the list.
The world I am looking for is something that cannot be linked back to him no matter what—something he just heard about in a random conversation and never bothered to think about again.
A world so deep in his memories that even he himself wouldn’t be able to recall it.

And while he did have quite a few conversations about many worlds, most of those worlds were visited by people who could be somehow linked back to him, no matter how weak that link was," Nux answered.
At his words, Vyriana frowned.
She understood Nux’s reasoning. If the worlds could be linked to him, then they could also be linked to her sisters. Vyriana knew that Nux wanted to avoid that, but…
"Aren’t you being too careful? I feel like you are limiting yourself.
Nux, you need to understand that we were lucky to get our hands on a Primordial from a Middle-Level World during this war. We will not be this fortunate every time.
If we follow your criteria, we might end up completely halting our progress. Everything we have done so far would become meaningless.
There are dangers around, especially the dangers of the unknown, but this doesn’t mean we stop walking."
At those words, Nux smiled wryly.
"You underestimate the Universe, my Dragon."
Then, he stared at her and said,
"Think of it like this:

To the Universe, when a world is ’destroyed,’ it doesn’t matter since everything would return to it, and it would simply create another world. It is simply an exchange of energy for it where it doesn’t lose anything.
To the Universe, ’death’ or ’destruction’ is all the same as ’life’ and ’creation.’
However, every time I make a move and take something away from it, it truly loses it—something it absolutely loathes."
Nux then paused as he glanced at Vyriana and said,
"Now consider yourself:
If there is a thief in your house that is constantly stealing your things, and no matter what you do, you are unable to catch him…
What would you do?
Would you give up and let him steal anything he wants?
Or… would you destroy your house, leaving nothing for him to steal because you know you can simply ’reform’ your house all brand new?"
Vyriana widened her eyes as she stared at Nux with a shocked look on her face.
Nux nodded.
"I do not know how the Universe thinks.

However, I do know that while it cannot self-destruct just to be recreated again since that would require too much energy, there is a high chance that it will destroy everything that has even the slightest link to the ’thief’ in order to try and catch him."
"Then…
Doesn’t that mean Yrniel is in danger…?"

chapters.title: Chapter 1860: Let’s spar.
paragraphs: "Then…
Doesn’t that mean Yrniel is in danger…?"
Vyriana spoke as if she had a revelation.
After all, Yrniel was still the closest link the Universe had to the ’thief.’
If it is prepared to destroy everything related to the thief, then…
Won’t it destroy Yrniel as well…?
At her words, Nux smiled wryly as well.
"Why else do you think I am trying to lay low and divert its attention so desperately?"
Nux glanced at the Primordial he threw away, and with a solemn look on his face, he continued,
"The Universe hasn’t lost much yet, so it shouldn’t be as desperate as I mentioned. This is why I plan to overwhelm it.
I will devour five worlds, one after another. After that,
I will devour around 15 random beings, all from the same world, to divert the Universe’s attention to that world.

Then, I will wait and see how it reacts, and if it consumes that world, I will devour 15 more beings, once again, from a single world. I will continue this till the Universe stops consuming worlds recklessly, even if I have to use up all my ’Space’ for it."
Nux revealed his plan, and Vyriana stared at him, taken aback by his words.
"I will overwhelm the Universe. I will confuse it to the point it would completely forget about Yrniel.
I will only leave two options for it:
Either give up on catching the ’thief,’𝒇𝓻𝓮𝓮𝙬𝙚𝒃𝒏𝓸𝙫𝒆𝙡.𝓬𝓸𝒎
Or self-destruct."
Nux’s golden eyes shined intensely as he said those words.
In just a single statement, he mentioned the destruction of more than ten worlds and billions of lives.
Yes, he was that desperate.
For himself… for his wives…
He would become the Ultimate Villain if need be.
The Ultimate Villain who would cause havoc in the entirety of the Universe.
And all this while…
His wives would be innocently participating in wars, having no hand in anything that was happening.
They would be the incarnations of innocence itself.
"You have been thinking about it all this while…?"
Vyriana questioned, her surprise couldn’t be hidden.
This… this was Nux…
He was a man who hated thinking things through and acted on what his heart desired.
Heck, this man once challenged the fearsome Dragon Lord without thinking of the consequences because that man hurt his wife, but now…
Just a few hours ago, instead of killing a man who entered his wife’s shadow like he would usually do, he waited and planned to make an example out of him later.

Not just that, instead of directly taking the weapon that would make him a threat even for a Transcendent, he thought of the possible consequences—consequences most wouldn’t even be able to think about, let alone consider—and decided to abandon the weapon.
Nux…
He was growing…
He was becoming a schemer who thought everything through before making a decision.
And Vyriana found it… extremely uncharacteristic.
But then,
"Hmm? What do you mean?"
Nux turned towards her with a frown.
"All this time?
No, I just thought of it a few minutes ago.
Seems like a good way to deal with the situation."
He replied, and Vyriana’s mouth twitched.

She clenched her fists, wanting to punch this bastard away from her, but his embrace was too comforting. Especially how he caressed her abdomen gently—her body was stimulated with a bit too much comfort for her to even think of moving right now.
But it’s okay…
She will get him next time…

paragraphs: "Hahahaha~
Did she actually say that? In front of everyone?
That’s so embarrassing; I have no clue how you didn’t chew her head off right then and there!"
"You look down on me if you think I would let her go that easily!"
"Hahaha! That’s my boy! I knew you wouldn’t disappoint me."
"Mhm, as they say, the fiercer they are, the tastier they taste."
"Especially her, she looked so fierce when she jumped at us with her swor—"
"Oi, I won her fair and square. We had a deal."
"Oh, come on, I’m not trying to steal her from you. Why are you acting so defensive, anyway? You’d be bored within a month, anyway."
"I doubt she’d last a month."
"Hahaha! What do you plan to do with her?"
"I don’t know. I’ve kept her in the Cage of Samsara for now. I’ll decide when we return."
"Cage of Samsara? Kakaka, you sick fuck! She wouldn’t even last a week! Hahahaha!"

A group of six-foot-tall monstrous beings laughed as they casually strolled together. These beings had humanoid bodies, but their appearance was nothing short of grotesque. Their skin was rough and grayish, plated like armor. Their eerie orange eyes glowed faintly in the dim light.

They had long faces with mouths filled with jagged teeth, as if they were created solely to tear flesh. Horns jutted from their foreheads, and their clawed hands clutched large weapons crafted for brutality.
They were Drakkars.
*Picture*
The Drakkars came from a low-level world named Gorath, a world at war with another low-level world, Secra. Secra housed one of the most densely populated races in the entire universe: humans.
A year ago, Gorath had launched an all-out attack on Secra, and today, the long war was finally over.
The result?
Gorath’s victory.
Yes, despite Secra’s Will blessing the humans, while they were able to put up a resistance at first, they eventually fell to Gorath’s cruel might.
The atmosphere stood in stark contrast to the Drakkars’ joyful mood.
The once-vibrant plains were now coated in blood and ash. The air reeked of iron and death, and the cries of the wounded had long since faded into an unsettling silence.
There was blood and corpses all over the place, corpses that didn’t just belong to the Humans but also to the Drakkar soldiers. It was clear from the sight that the war was a brutal one.

The human soldiers who were left alive knelt in neat rows on the bloodied ground, their faces covered with blood, mud, and despair. Their armors, once bright and strong, were now dented, torn, and stained.
One of the Drakkar from this group, who saw the human soldiers in such a state, laughed out loud.
"So much for the ’proud Secra warriors,’ look at them kneeling with their heads down. Hahaha! Fucking cowards."
He cursed.
"Hahaha!"
The rest of the group laughed out loud as well.
The human soldiers, however, kept their heads down, their mouths clenched. There was nothing they could say against those words.
Yes, they were cowards.
Instead of choosing to die like their allies, they decided to kneel and surrender… willingly.
It was humiliating, but the fear of death bent even the strongest of wills.
Another Drakkar stepped forward, tapping the flat of his blade against the chin of one kneeling human.

"Tell me, little soldier, how did it feel to watch your allies being executed while you knelt on the ground and lowered your head in shame? I wish to know, since, you know, I’ve never felt such a thing before.
Hahaha!
Come on, come on, tell us.
Did you cry for your king? Or did you scream for your mother?"
The human soldier said nothing.
"YOU DARE IGNORE ME!!?"
The Drakkar screamed in rage as he swung his blade. The human closed his eyes, his body trembling continuously.
"Don’t kill me! Don’t kill me!"
He shouted. Then, with his face covered in desperation, he stared at the Drakkar.
"I-I cried! I screamed for my mother! But no one came to help me! I was helpless! I was weak! Humans are weak! We were born weak!"
The soldier spoke, his body trembling without stop.
"Pathetic,"
A female Drakkar snorted as she turned around. She had no intention of getting involved with these weaklings.
But then, her eyes fell on something strange.
On the bloodied ground, she saw a thin wisp of black mist curling through the air.
It looked like smoke emitted from flames, just very… dark…
No…
Something was wrong.
There were no flames in this region.
However, before the Drakkar could think too much about it, the ’smoke’ dispersed, vanishing into nothingness.
"What the hell was that…?"
She muttered out loud.
"Hmm? Grania? What’s wrong?"
Another Drakkar soldier questioned. Enjoy more content from freewebnovel
Grania, the female Drakkar, glanced at him. Then, after thinking for a second, she shrugged.
"It was nothing."
The war was over, she was tired, and she wanted to return home. She didn’t have the energy to think too much about something so small.
Yes, she decided to ignore it.
It was a mistake.

Well, not that she could have done anything to stop what was going to happen anyway. It didn’t matter if it was her, her fellow comrades, her leaders, or the forces she was linked to, they were all helpless, oblivious to what was about to come.
The ’End’ had begun.
The atmosphere shifted. The laughing Drakkars stopped as their eyes fell on a single figure standing among the kneeling humans.
The figure was a human male, wearing torn and bloodied armor. His head hung low, and his body stood like a puppet.
At first, they thought it was just a soldier who, for some reason, had lost his mind and had risen to his feet.
"Huh? What’s this? Hey! Who bound them!? How did this one manage to set free!?"
A Drakkar shouted as he then turned towards the standing soldier.
"You! Kneel!"
He ordered. However, seeing that the human didn’t listen, he narrowed his eyes before a wide grin appeared on his face.
"So eager to have your flesh torn into pieces, eh? Well, then don’t blame me."
He laughed, but as he was about to rush towards the human,
"Wait."
Grania stopped him.
"Huh? What’s wrong?"
The Drakkar questioned. Grania, however, ignored his words as she stared at the human and narrowed her eyes.
She could sense it now.
Something was wrong.
The human’s skin was pale, almost gray. Grania also saw dark veins all across his exposed flesh.
The normal humans… they didn’t look like this.
And as if on cue, the human soldier raised his head.
Grania froze. The human’s eyes were lifeless, a milky white devoid of pupils. There were dark veins all over his face, just like his body.
It was then Grania realized it.
He was not alive.
"He’s… he’s a corpse,"
She muttered, instinctively taking a step back.
The zombie tilted its head, a cracking sound accompanying the motion.
Then, without warning, it lunged forward with a sword in its hand. A giant Drakkar kicked it away before he tore its head off.
"What the hell is happening?"
He questioned, confused.
But then,
"WATCH OUT!!"
Grania shouted as she tried to rush towards him. However, it was already too late as suddenly, six more zombies jumped on top of the giant Drakkar, overwhelming him with numbers.
"W-What are these things!? How are the dead soldiers moving!?"
The Drakkars screamed in horror.
The horror, however, had just begun. Suddenly, Grania saw that dark mist again. This time, it was much, much denser than before.
And before she could make sense of it,
"Grrrr…"
One by one, the lifeless corpses on the ground rose, their eyes pale and lifeless, their flesh covered in dark veins, and their bodies now driven by some otherworldly force.
What’s worse?
It wasn’t just the human corpses that were moving.
The Drakkar corpses were the same.
More and more corpses stood up as the dark mist around the area became denser and denser, enshrouding everything.
At first, the soldiers of Secra saw this as hope. They didn’t know what was happening, but they sure knew the Drakkars were going to have a bad day.
Whoever was behind this, it was their ally.
And as if to prove that theory, one of the corpses walked toward the kneeling soldier.
"T-These chains! Free me from these chains and I will be able to jo-"
The soldier tried to explain, but before he could do so,
Pierce
A sword pierced through his heart, killing him in an instant. And as his body fell on the ground, it rose up again, this time as one of the undead.
The Drakkars stared at the scene in horror.
"SOLDIERS OF GORATH!!"
Suddenly, they heard a loud cry.
It was one of the Drakkar army commanders.
"Prepare for battle!!
Crush the enemies, no matter what they are!!"
BOOOOM
The order was given, and in an instant, the Gorath soldiers prepared themselves. Their Auras burst out, ready to instantly overwhelm whatever those things were.
But then,
Suddenly, something even more horrifying happened.
The soldiers’ Aura…
It was canceled out.𝐟𝐫𝕖𝗲𝘄𝚎𝗯𝕟𝐨𝕧𝐞𝚕.𝕔𝕠𝐦
