chapters.title: Chapter 1862: Hmmm, I need better control.
paragraphs: "W-What!? How did that happen!?"
The Drakkar soldiers shouted in horror.
If the enemy had resisted their Auras using their own, they would have understood, but… for their Aura to simply… dissipate…
This made no sense.
The Drakkars, however, didn’t have time to think about this; the corpses were coming.
"Attack them!"
The commander ordered, and the Drakkars rushed forward, their weapons gleaming as they slashed and stabbed the corpses.
The corpses were easier to deal with; these beings couldn’t use their Laws.
But…
"Grrr…"
It didn’t make a difference.
All the corpses that were stabbed moved like it didn’t make a difference, and instead of defending, they attacked back.
Even the zombies that were slashed didn’t stop; their severed limbs twitched and crawled across the ground, and headless bodies continued their assault.
It was a horrifying sight.
Even Drakkars, who represented brutality and cruelty, felt deep fear rooting in them.
A fear that seeped into their bodies far too quickly than it should have… almost… unnaturally quickly.
It was as if… some being had used an ability that amplified their fear.
’He is a Prismorn. He can manipulate emotions, amplifying fear, courage, or joy.’
Nux recalled the being he had devoured before, and as he used his ability, combined with Astral Bond that provided him with almost unlimited energy…
The effect was… mind-blowing.
"AAAGGGGGHHHHH!!!!
WHAT THE HELL ARE THESE THINGS!!!"
The Drakkars screamed in horror; their morale couldn’t be any lower.
It wasn’t just Nux’s ability that amplified their fear; the Law of Absolute Death, which allowed Nux to use corpses, was simply too strong.
In a place that was filled with corpses, wherever the Drakkars looked, they saw corpses—corpses that came after them without considering their own defenses.

There were barely a thousand of them here who had managed to regroup properly, and they were facing an undying army ten times bigger than them. And… this army continued to rise in number as the Death Energy around them got denser and more Drakkars died.
What’s worse?
These corpses were covered with some sort of poisonous dark mist that not only kept them alive but also ate away at the Drakkars’ life force if they got too close.
"Commander! There are too many of them! We are unable to kill them!!"
The soldiers cried, trying their best to get away from the enemies. Even running away wasn’t possible because they were surrounded.
"Commander! What do we do!? We need reinforcements!!"
The soldiers shouted, but seeing that the commander wasn’t here, they frowned, and then someone shouted.
"The Commander ran away!!!"
"WHAT!?"
"THAT BASTARD!!!"
"Coward!!"
The soldiers couldn’t believe it.
"What do we do!?"
"Do you think we have another choice!? Fight!"
"Fight! Fight! Do not try to kill them! Push them away! Create a pathway!! Do not engage until absolutely necessary! We cannot win! We need to g-AAGGGHHHHH!!!!"

In the end, the soldiers had no way to resist. Yes, they all had their Laws, but their Aura didn’t work, and even if their Law strengthened them, against such overwhelming numbers and no strategy since everything just started randomly, it was only a matter of time before they fell.
"Haaah… Haahh… Haahh…"
On the other side, the commander who ran away from the battle breathed heavily.
No, he was not tired. He was a Peak Sovereign; he wouldn’t get tired from a little run.
He was horrified.
Unlike his soldiers, who were surrounded by all those corpses and had their vision limited…
He saw it…
That black mist…
It didn’t originate in that little town…
It came there… from the outskirts…
And that ’outskirt’ where it came from…
It was completely covered with that dense black mist to the point nothing else was visible. A few thousand…?
That was just the start…
There were about hundreds of thousands of those corpses in the outskirts that were all walking towards the town.
The soldiers would be overwhelmed no matter what they did.
He needed to do something! Anything!
He tried contacting the Leaders. Their army had a total of five Leaders, all at the Primordial Level. Two died in the war, but the other three were still here.
What the commander found strange was that even when he tried to contact them using the artifact, they didn’t reply.
Even when he tried to contact the rest of the commanders, a few of them did answer back, but their voices were unclear, and the connection was quickly cut off.
Things couldn’t be more obvious.
The enemy was hindering their communication.
And it made sense, after all,
Whoever was behind it, they wouldn’t want the Leaders to find out.
So the commander made a decision: he needed to get to Shakral, the capital of Secra, where the leaders were resting and inform them about what’s happening.
Yes, he was not running away because he was scared.
He was running away to deliver information.
Yes, he was not scared at all; he was just a responsible commander.
In the war between Secra and Gorath, millions of soldiers had perished… if they all…
Just imagining that scene sent shivers down his spine.
Yes, the Leaders needed to know what was happening as quickly as possible, and he was the only one who could do it.
He was the only one who could save his men and help them regroup.
"Haaahh… haahhh… haahh…"
As he justified his action, his breathing became heavier and heavier.
His body felt heavy; his limbs ached, screaming in protest. They were in no condition to run anymore.
It was obvious. He had already covered thousands of kilometers. It was normal for him to feel a bit tired.
Not to mention that the number of undead all while he rushed towards the capital had already reached half a million.
An overwhelming number that made his heart heavy and messed with his emotional state.
His body was simply reciprocating his emotional state and was getting tired…
Yes, it was completely normal…
"Haaahh… Haahh… Haahh…"
The commander continued to breathe. His heart raced, his lungs felt as if they were on fire, but then, the commander suddenly stopped.
Something was wrong.
He… he shouldn’t be tired…
It was merely a few thousand kilometres, he had barely been running for a few minutes, he would never be tired so quickly, even if he ran with one leg.
Something was messing with his mind…
"Haaahh… Haahh… Haahh…"
The commander looked around, trying to figure it out, and then, he noticed another thing…
As his breaths came in ragged gasps, each of his exhales formed small clouds of mist.
"Cold…?"
He whispered with a frown on his face.
Something was wrong.
Secra was a warm world, the temperature here was always high to the point where beings with cold elements were extremely weakened.
Then…
Why did he feel so cold…?

The commander looked ahead, the Shakral’s Walls were now visible to him. They were only about a few hundred kilometres away. Soon, however, the commander narrowed his eyes as he noticed something else…
The walls…
They had a layer of ice covering them?
"Ice?"
The commander frowned.
However, before he could think too much, he heard a voice.
"Grr…"
It was the zombies.
Hundreds of thousands of them, it was as if they had consumed all the towns behind them and were now coming for him.
The commander widened his eyes in horror as he ran away!
’NO!’
His mind shuddered.
In an instant, his body that was ’tired’ recovered.
’I need to get to the leaders to survive!’
With that thought in his mind, he started running. Ignoring everything he saw in the way.

The road beneath his feet that had started to be covered by a thin layer of frost, his breathing that was getting more and more ragged, his body that felt heavier and heavier, he ignored everything and ran.
"Grr…"
As he reached the capital and jumped over the giant walls, the distance between him and the zombies widened. He, however, didn’t stop.
He ignored the fact that the capital had turned into a domain of ice where all the beings, Humans and Drakkars alike, had turned into ice statues, and rushed towards the very centre of the capital.
"Haaahh… Haahh… Haahh…"
His breathing became heavier and heavier, some of the frost had started to cover his body. This, however, didn’t stop him, he quickly barged into the largest building in the capital and shouted,

"Lord Gorr! Something’s happening! The world’s temperature is falling! The entire capital has turned into ice! The communication artifacts are not working! The corpses are moving and overwhelming the soldiers! And they are making their way here!
We need to burn the enemy Primordials’ corpses to ashes so they won’t attack us and find a way to deal with those corpses!"
The commander reported everything in one breath. However, the moment he raised his head to glance at the leaders…
He saw a sight he would never forget in his life. Continue reading at freewebnovel

An extremely handsome human stood with Secra’s Core in one hand. With the other, he was holding Lord Gorr’s body by its neck. He was stepping on Lord Zaros’s body while Lord Grimm’s body was nowhere to be seen.
"Huh…?"
The human then turned towards him with a frown on his face and,
"You managed to come here?

Was creating an Ice Domain, increasing gravity, manipulating everyone’s emotions, covering the entire world with Death Energy, using necromancy to deal with the scrubs, and fighting three Primordials all at the same time too much?"
The man wondered out loud.
Then, as if the human came up with an answer, he nodded to himself and glanced at him.
"Your will to survive must be stronger than others. You were able to break free of the emotional wall I created for you people.
Congratulations."
Nux nodded. Then, as if he was done with the man, he turned away, and before the commander could react, he felt some sort of force surround his body and,
BOOOM
His body burst into pieces.
"Hmmm, I need better control."
Nux muttered to himself and then, he stared at the white ball in his hand and shrugged.
"Meh, let’s eat first."

chapters.title: Chapter 1863: Time and Space Rifts
paragraphs: "Haaaahhh… Haahhhh… Haaaaahhhh…"
An extremely beautiful blue-haired woman with golden eyes breathed heavily, her ample breasts moved up and down. Her clothes, wet from her sweat, stuck to her body, enhancing her curves.
"Haaahh… Haahh… Haahh…"

The woman’s golden eyes looked tired. She bent down as she placed her hands on her knees, gasping for air—a posture that further enhanced her cleavage. It was a sight that could seduce any man in the world.
However, despite all that, this wasn’t the most attractive part of her body. It was the Fox Ears and Eight Fluffy Fox Tails that melted a man’s heart.
A heaven, pure, blissful heaven.
Yes, the woman was Vulpiana Dawnshade, and currently, she was in a training hall, pushing herself to the limit.
"Haaaahhhh…"
The fox took a deep breath again. Then, she stood up straight and lifted her hand.
The space in front of her distorted, and she created what looked like a special rift. Then, the number of rifts started increasing.
One, two, three…
In total, six rifts were formed. Then,
After taking another deep breath, Vulpiana jumped into one of them and, in an instant,

Six Vulpianas appeared, jumping out of all the rifts. The six of them tried to use their swords, attempting to attack the puppet that stood in the middle. However, all their shots missed, and the puppet remained unharmed.
Of course, Vulpianas didn’t give in. They continued to attack until suddenly, one of the clones seemed to slip and got too close to the rift she had created before.
Then suddenly,
Whoosh

The rift’s extremely strong suction force pulled her in. That instant seemed to have triggered something as suddenly, all the rifts released extremely strong suction pulls, pulling all the Vulpianas in.

As Vulpiana’s bodies were pulled into the rift, they were thrown out of another. The intensity of that movement, however, was so strong that Vulpiana, who was thrown out, would then be unable to resist the pull of another rift and would be thrown out again from another rift, only for the process to continue.
And this was happening to six Vulpianas at the same time.
"Aaaaahhhhhhhh!!!!"

Trapped in the loop, Vulpiana could only shout as her body was squashed and stretched by the rifts. One by one, the number of Vulpianas continued to increase, and within 5 minutes, the entire area inside the rifts was filled with Vulpianas, who were continuously being pulled into and thrown out of the rifts.
The entire hall thundered with hundreds of Vulpianas screaming in pain and frustration, until finally, she ran out of energy, and the rifts, together with the other Vulpianas, started disappearing.
The only ones left were the puppet, which had already been thrown out of the area, and Vulpiana, who lay on the floor.
"AAaaggghhhhh…"
Groaning in pain, she grabbed her head as if wanting to burst it open to end all of this.
As the pain started receding, she turned around, her face facing the ceiling, her breathing ragged.
"Haaahh… Haaahh… Haahh…"
Her body was now covered with even more sweat. Even in this situation, the woman looked absolutely alluring.
Just that… she was simply too tired and in pain to think about all this.
"That looks painful."
Suddenly, a voice was heard.

Vulpiana didn’t even bother raising her head to see who it was. After all, there were only two people here most of the time. She had now interacted with this person so many times that she would recognize her voice even in her sleep. Find your next read at freewebnovel
"Hmmm? Why are you silent? Are you in a bad mood?"
The voice questioned again as it got closer and closer until Vulpiana finally saw a face.
It was another woman whose beauty simply couldn’t be described by words. Purple hair, purple eyes, purple horns, a face that was no short of perfection, and a body…
A body so sinful that even the loose gown couldn’t hide her curves.
A walking seductress, a woman who could bring any man to his knees just with her presence alone.
The Previous Queen of all Succubi, Eisheth.
"Try seeing the vision and hearing independent thoughts of hundreds of you, then we will talk."𝘧𝑟𝑒𝑒𝘸𝘦𝘣𝑛𝑜𝘷𝑒𝓁.𝘤𝘰𝓂
Vulpiana answered.
"Mhm, it looked painful before, now it even sounds painful."
The Succubus chuckled.
"Also, you said you only wanted to try it with six. Why did you increase the numbers so much?"
She questioned, and the tired Vulpiana raised her head to look into the Queen’s eyes.
"Did I look like I did that on purpose or had any form of control over it?"
"Well, it is your Law…"
Eisheth answered, and Vulpiana’s mouth twitched.
"So? What happened?"
Eisheth questioned seriously.

"Nothing. You mess with time, and it happens. The rift distorts the time and space around a region. Because of the instability of time and space, when I jump into it, it displaces me to another region but keeps that ’instant’s me’ inside, making it possible for me to come out of another rift."
"Language."
Eisheth smiled kindly.
She didn’t understand anything.
Vulpiana sighed.

"The distorted time and space in the area allow me to be at more than one place at the same time. I wanted to limit the number to six, but because I still do not have control over it, it created too many versions of ’me’ at the same time, and this happened."
She made it as simple as she could.
"So… clones?"
Eisheth frowned.
It seemed like a complicated ability, but…
If the end result was just clones… then wasn’t it practically useless?
After all, even a random incubus could create clones.
Vulpiana, however, shook her head.
"They are not clones. They are all me.
They are all real me."
"Then why are you the only one left? Where did the rest of them go?"
"They disappeared because my energy ran out."
"See? That means you are the real one."
Vulpiana, however, shook her head.
"You do not understand. They were all me of that ’instance.’ They were all real."
To make it simpler for the Succubus Queen, Vulpiana used another example.
"In a battle, if the opponent kills every single one of my instances except one, that one would be me.
It will not ’become’ me. It will be me."
"So you are saying…
If you hide one of all hundreds of ’you,’
You are immortal?"
"Yes."
Vulpiana nodded, and Eisheth stared at the woman, her mouth agape.
"And… this is just one of your Law’s applications, while its real implication actually allows you to hide?"
"Yes."

It will be me."

You are immortal?"

"And… this is just one of your Law’s applications, while its real implication actually allows you to hide?"
"Yes."

"Normal is boring anyways."

"What could a normal person even do?
Rule a state? Be the strongest in your state, with absolute authority, a power where no one would defy your words, power to control everyone’s life and death?
Been there, done that.
And let me tell you, girl.
It’s boring.
That is what normal is."
Eisheth declared.
Yes, the previous queen had a very different definition of normal.
Then, she glanced at Vulpiana and,

Now compare it with a crazy life.
A life where your head isn’t normal.

A life where the only thing you think about is that one man, and just the thought of him alone fills you with endless happiness. "That man isn’t even here."
She retorted.
"Are you missing him?
Do you want me to call him?"
Eisheth questioned.
"Well, it is not that easy, Mother.

"You are back."

Aisha replied with a big smile on her face. Then, suddenly,
"Aisha."
Vulpiana called out.
"Take me with you.
I wish to participate in the next war."

paragraphs: "Take me with you.
I wish to participate in the next War."
Vulpiana spoke with a determined look on her face.
She had given a lot of thought into this and had considered every possibility, even the possibility of her dying, but even then, she wanted to participate. She was prepared to face everything.
"You are too weak, you will die."
Completely disregarding her determination, Aisha spoke as she waved her hand continuously.
"Then make me a Divine."
Vulpiana, of course, didn’t give in and demanded.
"Huh?"
Aisha raised her eyebrows.
"Doesn’t Nux have the ability to turn me into a Divine Stage Cultivator?"
Vulpiana countered, and hearing those words, Aisha glanced at Eisheth. The previous Queen, however, just smiled back.𝐟𝚛𝕖𝚎𝕨𝗲𝐛𝚗𝐨𝐯𝐞𝕝.𝐜𝗼𝗺
Vulpiana then turned towards Eisheth and,
"Didn’t you say he would come anytime you want him to? Call him now, I wish to see him."
"I didn’t know you had such a dominant side~"
Eisheth chuckled.
"Call him."
Vulpiana demanded, but,
"Did you not hear what I said? He is busy right now."
Hearing those words, Vulpiana, who was staring at Eisheth, didn’t even turn towards Aisha and remarked sarcastically,
"And I thought he was never too busy to see his wives."
"You are not his wife."
Aisha didn’t back down either.
"She is one."
Vulpiana replied as she pointed at Eisheth.
"Or are you saying you do not wish to see him?"
The fox’s lips rose up in a mocking manner.
Her tricks, however, were useless in front of the previous Queen.
Eisheth was on a completely different wavelength.
"See? I told you she is quite good. Doesn’t her intensity match Amaya’s?"
Eisheth spoke as she turned towards her daughter.
"You think that’s comparable to that woman…?"
Aisha couldn’t believe what she was hearing.
"Mother, you haven’t seen half of it.
When that woman gets desperate…"
Aisha thought about it, and her spine felt weak momentarily,
"Well, let’s just say she gets quite dangerous…
Even Vyriana and Astaria avoid her during those moments. You should do that too, okay?"
The daughter was looking out for her mother.
"Is that so…?"
Eisheth was taken aback. Soon, however, she nodded in realization.
"Yes, she was a messed-up woman even back then."
Eisheth had once taken a slight glimpse into the women’s heads the first time she met them. Even if she didn’t read their memories, that little glimpse was enough for her to know what she needed.
"For such a woman to have all that power… it is quite dangerous indeed."
Eisheth commented, understanding what her daughter was trying to say.
Yes, the mother and daughter had started judging their husband’s wife, completely ignoring the Fox who stood right next to them, trying to get their attention.
In the end, Vulpiana burst out.
"This is why I say I never understand you, Eisheth!
You were a Queen! A Queen! And to think you have turned into… this!
It is shameful!

It is as if you no longer have any ambition! You just stay back in this jail while you wait for your ’husband’ to return every once in a while and give you attention! You cannot even call him when you want to!
Even Lyriana, who isn’t even his wife, has already gotten so much more powerful than before now that she is with him, but you are just… a waste!"
At those words, Aisha’s expression changed.
"Whatever she has ’turned into,’ she is much better than an incompetent spy."
She spoke. This time, there were no traces of amusement in her tone.
"I can only imagine how brazen one needs to be to let out her frustration on the only woman who bothers to talk to you.
Why don’t you go and confront that mother of yours!?"
Aisha shouted.
"Aisha…"
Eisheth called out. Aisha, however, turned towards her mother and,
"Please, Mother. Let me say it."
"A bunch of incompetent people who couldn’t even protect their own race, and the race’s leader resorts to sending her daughter somewhere else to try and protect her."
Aisha then glared at Vulpiana and,
"And now the daughter tries to act like this in front of people trying to protect her.
Pathetic."
Vulpiana turned silent. Her body trembled as she clenched her fists.
Aisha, on the other hand, just snorted. She wanted to take her mother and go away in order to let this woman rot alone, but then,
"Hmm? What’s with the strange environment? Did something happen?"

Nux, who walked out of a portal, questioned with a strange look on his face. Of course, as confused as he was, he didn’t forget to appear next to Eisheth and embrace the previous Queen like it was his birthright.
Feeling Eisheth’s soft body all over him filled him with a strong sense of warmth and comfort.
"You are back."
Eisheth spoke in a light tone, a smile automatically appearing on her face.
"Of course, I came back early because I missed you."
"I don’t sense it…?"
Eisheth frowned.
But then,
RUMBLE RUMBLE RUMBLE
THUNDER THUNDER THUNDER
The Universe trembled in anger.
It had lost another one of its Worlds.
"Do you sense it now?"
Nux chuckled as he pulled Eisheth even closer, sniffing her scent.
Eisheth’s body squirmed, she arched her back, rubbing her butt on Nux’s crotch, trying to tempt him.
Aisha, who saw her mother instantly forgetting everything that just happened, sighed. Then,
"Nux! I am here too!"
She jumped on Nux.
She wanted another session together with her mother!
Nux, of course, could never deny his wives and opened his arm for Aisha to jump in. But then suddenly,
"Nux."
Vulpiana called out. Her golden eyes stared at the man with determination.
"Make me a Divine Stage Cultivator. I promise I will not disappoint you."
"Hmm?"
Nux tilted his head for a moment. Then, he nodded.
"Alright, I hope you keep your promise."
"What…?"
Vulpiana widened her eyes in disbelief.
"What?"
Nux frowned.
"Are you… agreeing?"
"Yeah? Should I not?"
"That easily…?"
Vulpiana couldn’t believe it.
Nux, on the other hand, grinned evilly.
"Were you expecting me to demand something in return?
What are you willing to do, Vulpiana Dawnshade?"

chapters.title: Chapter 1867: What do you plan to do with her?
paragraphs: Two Sovereign Level Beings stood together, their backs nearly sticking together as they covered for each other.
Both of them were surrounded by more than fifteen Sovereigns prepared to kill them. However, these fifteen were not what these two were worried about.
They had an entirely different problem.
"W-What are these women!? Where did they come from!? Do something about them!"
Stay updated via freewebnovel
One of them shouted.
"What am I supposed to do!? Do you even hear yourself!? Do you not see them!?"
The other retorted.
"I AM seeing them! This is why I am telling you to do something! If this continues, it will be over!"
"And how do you expect me to take care of them!? Every single one of them is an absurdity! That woman who controls blood over there massacred my entire unit and turned them into her soldiers!"

"You do not understand! She is nothing! My men asked me if they should target the one who carries the sword because they thought she was one of the weaker ones. I agreed. Although it was a pity to use so many men to deal with one woman, I still allowed it since that might affect the morale of the rest, but…
One strike.
That woman killed all my men in one strike!
She then looked into my eyes as if knowing that I was the one who sent that army.
And do you know what she did after that!?
She walked away!
I swear to the lord that I saw her mouth ’Too Far’ before she started killing people closer to her with a bored look on her face.
The only reason I survived was because I was too far! That woman didn’t even consider me a threat big enough to move and deal with on her own!"
Yes, the being was extremely shaken.
"The others aren’t any weaker either, especially that one!"
He pointed at the General hovering in the air, looking down on the battlefield.
She was the worst!
His body trembled as he realized what sort of monstrosity they were facing. Ever since the battle began, these women were never at a disadvantage.
It was a WAR, goddammit!
How is this even possible for them to not feel overwhelmed even once!?
But then, the two heard a voice.
"HAHAHAHA!!
I GOT ONE!"

With hopeful eyes, they turned and saw one of their allies who had appeared right behind a woman with purple eyes and hair, who was busy dealing with four Sovereigns and had no idea he was next to her.

Their eyes shined in expectation. They all knew they were going to die, but they wanted to at least kill one of these mercenaries before going to the afterworld, or at least see one die with their own eyes.
However, just as their wish was about to come true,
Pierce
A sword pierced through their ally’s chest, as a woman with fox-like ears appeared from God knows where and killed him without showing any expression on her face.

Sensing the movement behind her, Aisha turned around, and her eyes fell on Vulpiana. Looking at her bloodied sword and the dead being behind her, it didn’t take long for Aisha to realize what had happened. She, however, narrowed her eyes and stared at the fox.
"I will not thank you, Fox."
"I did not do it for your sake."
Vulpiana’s answer was quick.
"I did it for your mother. She will be sad if something happened to you."
"Those are some grand words from someone like you. Don’t think I forgot what you said that day."
Aisha wasn’t planning on giving up.
Vulpiana stared at the succubus and,
"I have apologized for what I did. This is a matter between Eisheth and me. You have no right to interfere."
"Of course, it is easier to apologize when you got what you wanted."
Aisha snorted.
Vulpiana turned silent.
Then suddenly,
Pierce
A sword pierced through the fox’s heart. Vulpiana, however, didn’t react to it. She simply glanced at Aisha and,
"Think whatever you wish. I will just say one thing, I am not your enemy."
"You are literally a spy!"
Aisha retorted as she beheaded the man who had attacked Vulpiana. The fox’s body fell on the ground, but she just laughed,
"And who am I supposed to report to? The ’incompetent’ leader of my race?"
As she said those words, her body disappeared.
Aisha, who was left alone, surrounded by enemies, screamed in anger as she released her Aura.
BOOOM
In an instant, she beheaded three of her enemies and,
’I still do not like her.’
She snorted.
’But you have to admit, she is strong.’
She heard Nux’s voice.
’Sister Astaria is strong as well.’
Aisha answered. Nux, however, shook his head.
’She is different. If she is hell-bent on hiding, even I would have a difficult time finding her, and I possess the knowledge of entire worlds.’
Nux answered.
Aisha turned silent, and Nux continued,
’It isn’t just a matter of ’quality of energy.’ Her Law would work even against beings of a higher phase.

One would need a mind capable of comprehending the concept of time and space to even know where she is hidden. As for being able to reach that place and capture her? That’s an entirely different matter.
I can assure you, even if I am not here and the Primordials decide to attack, she will survive. And this isn’t the end of it.
Her Law is much more powerful and would become even harder to deal with once she explores it even further.
Temporal Distortion, the ability to alter the flow of time around herself, her allies, or her enemies.
Rewind Edge, the ability to rewind her own movements within a short timeframe, undoing injuries or repositioning herself in combat.
Time Fractures, the ability to freeze time between two places, allowing her to pretty much teleport from one point to another.
Temporal Confinement, the ability to trap the enemy in a pocket of frozen time, making them immobile and unable to act for a set duration.
She has already learned all this.’
Nux praised, and this time, Aisha couldn’t help but frown.
’Nux…’
She called out.
’What do you plan to do with her?’
The succubus questioned. At her question, however, her shadow just trembled, showed her a thumbs-up, and winked at her,𝒇𝙧𝙚𝓮𝔀𝓮𝒃𝙣𝓸𝒗𝒆𝒍.𝙘𝒐𝒎
Not saying anything else.

chapters.title: Chapter 1868: Four Entities.
paragraphs: RUMBLE RUMBLE RUMBLE
THUNDER THUNDER THUNDER
Once again, the Universe trembled, wreaking havoc in millions of worlds. It was angry—extremely angry—but once again, there was nothing it could do.
It had even devoured an entire world that it thought was connected to the ’Anomaly,’ thinking it would stop the Anomaly, but it didn’t.
The Anomaly continued to steal more and more of what belonged to it, and it could not do anything.
RUMBLE RUMBLE RUMBLE
THUNDER THUNDER THUNDER
It roared again, this time causing even more havoc because of how enraged it was.

And while the Universe threw its tantrums, in a giant room, a large square-shaped table that covered the entire room was the only thing that could be seen. It was quite impractical—after all, the table left no space to keep anything else in this giant room.
However, one thing to note was that while the rest of the Universe trembled and worlds were crushed, this room was silent.
Let alone tremors, not a single thing here moved from its place. It was as if the Universe’s tantrums had no effect on this place.
Then, suddenly, on the four sides of the table, four ’entities’ emerged.
What did they look like? No one could tell.
It was as if it was a taboo for one to see these entities.
They could only ’feel’ their presence but not see them.
One of them had a calming presence that would put anyone at ease. The other was the complete opposite—its presence was filled with so much malice that it was suffocating to be around them.
The third being simply thrived in the middle, his presence radiating stillness and cruelty at the same time. As for the last entity…
It was simply too complicated to understand. The presence it radiated was… something incomprehensible, something that… shouldn’t exist…?
These entities couldn’t be put into mere words.
Then, suddenly, a voice was heard.
"It happened again."
The incomprehensible entity commented.
"The Universe is enraged…"
The calming entity nodded. It could feel the Universe’s emotions, and sensing those chaotic thoughts worried it.
"Did you find out what this Anomaly is?"
The entity of Malice questioned.
"I did not."
The incomprehensible entity denied.
"You did not, or were you unable to find it?"
The entity of Malice questioned back, its tone mocking.
"What about the Seer? Did you contact her? What did she say?"
The entity of Balance questioned, completely ignoring the entity of Malice’s words. Malice didn’t mind it either. It seemed like they were all already used to it.
"I did."
This time, the incomprehensible entity nodded.
However, the news wasn’t good.
"She says that if even the Universe cannot find the Anomaly, how could she? Her vision does not go beyond the Universe."
"The Universe is merely a Will, while she is a living entity. There is a difference between the two."
The calming entity spoke.
It didn’t question the incomprehensible entity since it knew that it must have mentioned the same point it did.
"She did not answer after my initial question."
The incomprehensible entity replied.
"That one is quite arrogant."
The entity of Malice commented arrogantly.
"You people do not mind if I kill her, do you?"
It questioned.
"Unnecessary killing should be avoided."
The calming entity frowned.
"Bah! I didn’t ask you in the first place!"
The entity of Malice snorted and turned toward the other two.
"You will not listen even if we say otherwise. What is the point of asking?"
The entity of Balance replied in a monotonous tone.
"It is fun to go against you."
The entity of Malice grinned.
"Kill her if you can find her."
The incomprehensible entity shrugged.
There was a reason these four entities even thought about bringing the Seer up for discussion—she was capable. It wasn’t easy to deal with her, even for them.
"This is not why we are gathered here."
Suddenly, the entity of Balance spoke up, its tone solemn.
"The Anomaly continues to make trouble and anger the Universe. At first, its actions were tamed, hidden even, but the Anomaly is getting more and more daring.
If this continues, the Universe might react, and if it does…
It would be difficult to predict what the outcome would be or who amongst the four of us will be selected."
Then, the entity frowned and,
"The Balance will be broken."
It commented.

If it were a normal situation, the rest of the entities—especially the entity of Malice—would have completely ignored the topic. Sure, for the calming entity, it may be a problem because the Anomaly came with countless deaths.
But for the incomprehensible entity, the Anomaly was a new target of knowledge. It would very much like to understand more of it, and to understand it, it would do its best to keep the Anomaly alive.
The entity of Malice was the same. The Anomaly came with death and destruction—a zone where it thrived. If anything, the Anomaly could become its ally.
However…
The problem was the Universe.
If the Universe reacted, the entity of Malice wasn’t sure if it would be the one who gets selected, and if it is not it, everything will crumble.
The incomprehensible entity had the same line of thought, and because of this, the four entities wanted to find the Anomaly and get rid of it.
"What should we do?" Continue reading on freewebnovel
The entity of Balance questioned again.
"The Anomaly is using the War as a veil. Should we stop the War?"
The calming entity suggested.
"No."
The first one to reject the idea was the entity of Malice.
"Ending the War would only result in the Anomaly going back into hiding again. Even the Universe and the Seer cannot find it—we won’t be able to either.
We need the War to keep the Anomaly active."
The incomprehensible entity commented.
"I say raise the stakes of the War."
The entity of Malice suggested, its tone visibly more excited.
"We will let the War continue as it is."
The incomprehensible entity decided.
"And we will look for that Anomaly.
Start with beings of higher Phases, and do not forget that arrogant man with the crimson mist. He protected the Anomaly once. He must be connected to it."

These entities couldn’t be put into mere words.
Then, suddenly, a voice was heard.
"It happened again."
The incomprehensible entity commented.
"The Universe is enraged…"
The calming entity nodded.
It could feel the Universe’s emotions, and sensing those chaotic thoughts worried it.
"Did you find out what this Anomaly is?"
The entity of Malice questioned.
"I did not."
The incomprehensible entity denied.
"You did not, or were you unable to find it?"
The entity of Malice questioned back, its tone mocking.
"What about the Seer?
Did you contact her?
What did she say?"
The entity of Balance questioned, completely ignoring the entity of Malice’s words.
Malice didn’t mind it either.
It seemed like they were all already used to it.
"I did."
This time, the incomprehensible entity nodded.
However, the news wasn’t good.
"She says that if even the Universe cannot find the Anomaly, how could she?
Her vision does not go beyond the Universe."
"The Universe is merely a Will, while she is a living entity.
There is a difference between the two."
The calming entity spoke.
It didn’t question the incomprehensible entity since it knew that it must have mentioned the same point it did.
"She did not answer after my initial question."
The incomprehensible entity replied.
"That one is quite arrogant."
The entity of Malice commented arrogantly.
"You people do not mind if I kill her, do you?"
It questioned.
"Unnecessary killing should be avoided."
The calming entity frowned.
"Bah!
I didn’t ask you in the first place!"
The entity of Malice snorted and turned toward the other two.
"You will not listen even if we say otherwise.
What is the point of asking?"
The entity of Balance replied in a monotonous tone.
"It is fun to go against you."
The entity of Malice grinned.
"Kill her if you can find her."
The incomprehensible entity shrugged.
There was a reason these four entities even thought about bringing the Seer up for discussion—she was capable.
It wasn’t easy to deal with her, even for them.
"This is not why we are gathered here."
Suddenly, the entity of Balance spoke up, its tone solemn.
"The Anomaly continues to make trouble and anger the Universe.
At first, its actions were tamed, hidden even, but the Anomaly is getting more and more daring.
If this continues, the Universe might react, and if it does…
It would be difficult to predict what the outcome would be or who amongst the four of us will be selected."
Then, the entity frowned and,
"The Balance will be broken."
It commented.
If it were a normal situation, the rest of the entities—especially the entity of Malice—would have completely ignored the topic.
Sure, for the calming entity, it may be a problem because the Anomaly came with countless deaths.
But for the incomprehensible entity, the Anomaly was a new target of knowledge.
It would very much like to understand more of it, and to understand it, it would do its best to keep the Anomaly alive.
The entity of Malice was the same.
The Anomaly came with death and destruction—a zone where it thrived.
If anything, the Anomaly could become its ally.
However…
The problem was the Universe.
If the Universe reacted, the entity of Malice wasn’t sure if it would be the one who gets selected, and if it is not it, everything will crumble.
The incomprehensible entity had the same line of thought, and because of this, the four entities wanted to find the Anomaly and get rid of it.

"The Anomaly is using the War as a veil.
Should we stop the War?"
The calming entity suggested.
"No."
The first one to reject the idea was the entity of Malice.
"Ending the War would only result in the Anomaly going back into hiding again.
Even the Universe and the Seer cannot find it—we won’t be able to either.
We need the War to keep the Anomaly active."
The incomprehensible entity commented.
"I say raise the stakes of the War."
The entity of Malice suggested, its tone visibly more excited.
"We will let the War continue as it is."
The incomprehensible entity decided.
"And we will look for that Anomaly.
Start with beings of higher Phases, and do not forget that arrogant man with the crimson mist.
He protected the Anomaly once.
He must be connected to it."

chapters.title: Chapter 1869: I need to see my daughter.
paragraphs: "Congratulations on your breakthrough, Queen Rislith."
The state nobles congratulated her as they all bowed their heads in front of the woman who sat on the throne.

She was the new Queen of the Lust State, the eldest daughter of the previous queen, Rislith Lust, and today, she had broken through and had become a Divine Stage Cultivator, stepping into the realm of the strongest.

Even before, when Queen Rislith was merely a Saint, the authority she had in the Lust State was absolute. After all, only her loyal subjects were able to become Saints because of Nux Leander’s help, not to mention the woman also had 25 Divine Stage Cultivators at her command, prepared to do anything she commanded them to.

But even then, questions about the current queen’s qualifications had been rising. Even though the voices were low, they were still there, especially after the Mana Apocalypse ended and mana returned to its normal state.

Countless people had broken through during this time. The speed of their breakthroughs was surprisingly fast. Some even wondered whether the quality of Yrniel’s mana had risen, while others simply reasoned that after the Mana Apocalypse, many started taking cultivation seriously, not wanting to suffer like they did before.
However, while the news of all these breakthroughs all over Yrniel was considered good, the new Succubus Queen was still a Saint. People were starting to have doubts.
But now…

Rislith crushed any seeds of doubt or rebellion that might have been forming. The nobles, who realized it, congratulated her with sincere hearts. After all, all of them were extremely loyal to the queen, especially after everything she had done for them.
"Be at ease."
Rislith nodded at her subjects.
"I believe there are no further matters left to discuss?"
She questioned. It was clear from her tone that she was long used to such things.
"Yes, My Queen."
One of her subjects nodded.
The queen nodded back.
"Then you are all dismissed."
"Yes, Your Majesty."
The nobles bowed their heads before they emptied the royal hall. Rislith sighed as she returned to her room as well.
However, the moment she walked in, her movements slowed down as she narrowed her eyes. Just as she was about to call the Divine Stage Slaves,
"You are quite perceptive. That is a good thing."
She heard a voice, and suddenly, an extremely beautiful woman appeared in front of the Queen of Succubi.
A woman Rislith knew well.
Faelara Dawnshade.
The head of the Foxkin.
And… the leader of the Black Order.
Yes, Rislith obviously knew the truth as well. After all, her mother and sister often visited her and told her many things.
Rislith was probably one of the most knowledgeable Yrniel leaders right now.
"What are you doing here?"
Rislith questioned as she narrowed her eyes.
At the same time, she commanded the slaves to return. After all, she knew the truth. She knew how strong Faelara actually was.
A complete Divine like her could easily crush the entire state, and they would be completely helpless against her.
"You are sharp."
Faelara commented with a smile.
"But don’t worry, I am not an enemy."
"I asked, what are you doing here?"
Rislith repeated her question.
"You are very unwelcoming."
Faelara complained.
"I tend to do that when people barge into my personal quarters unannounced."
"I admit, that was disrespectful of me. I didn’t wish to attract too much attention since I thought you probably would not want to link your state to the Dawnshade House.
But I apologize. I overstepped my boundaries."
Faelara admitted her mistake. Rislith, however, continued to stare at her, waiting for the answer to the question she asked earlier.
"You don’t like small talk, huh?"
Faelara muttered.
"Well, that is good for me."
She nodded. Then, the Dawnshade leader glanced at the Succubus Queen and,
"The reason I came here is simple.
I need to see my daughter."
"She is not here."
"I know that, of course. I know she is with that man, but I have no means to contact him."
"So you came here?"
"I couldn’t think of many other places."
Rislith turned silent, her mouth twitching.
How did she turn into a messenger? But in the end, she just shook her head and,
"I will deliver your message. Now please leave."
"You really are unwelcoming, aren’t you?"
Rislith stared at the fox. The fox chuckled and then,
"Well, I am grateful for your help.
Just tell them that it is quite urgent, so the earlier she can return, the better.
I will take my leave then."
After a slight nod, the woman disappeared, as if she was never here in the first place.
The room turned silent.
It was only after a minute that Rislith came out of her reverie and,
"I am surrounded by monsters."
She sighed.

Not wanting another such visit, she took out an artifact, and the instant she activated it, a portal appeared right in front of her, and another extremely beautiful woman walked out with a cheerful smile on her face.
"To think you would call for me yourself, I am glad~"
Eisheth chuckled as she hugged her eldest daughter.
Rislith hugged her back. Her mother’s embrace felt comfortable.
The two stayed like this for a while and then,
"So? What is it? Why did you call me?"
Eisheth knew her daughter well. There was no way she would call her using the artifact just because she missed her.
Not that she was letting her miss her anyway. Eisheth came here to bother her daughter every other week.
"The Dawnshade was here just now."
Stay connected with freewebnovel
Rislith answered, and in an instant, Eisheth’s face turned solemn.
"She was?"
Rislith nodded as she then told her everything that had happened.
"Hmmm. I guess Nux didn’t give her a way to contact him. He was probably expecting it."
"I bet he did it on purpose."
Rislith snorted.
"I can’t deny it…"
Eisheth couldn’t defend her husband.
"Tsk, that man is annoying."
"Cannot deny that either."
Eisheth chuckled.
Then, she nodded.
"Don’t worry, I’ll send Vulpiana to her mother.
Anyways, that aside,
You tell me, little girl.
Already a Divine, eh?"
"I am not a little girl."
"You will always be a little girl, little girl."

"Then we will be taking our leave now."
The leaders nodded, and once the mercenary women left, they all sighed.
"What a bunch of monsters," one of the leaders commented.
"The Leander Family, huh?"
"I still do not understand why beings of such caliber are working as mercenaries."
"Don’t treat them like normal mercenaries. They have won almost forty wars in the past six months. This number is already higher than what most parties boast.
Not to mention the fact that they have never once failed a single mission, no matter how difficult or whatever unexpected thing may have popped up.
They even have an army of their own a world could hire to fight for them.
It is said that if you manage to hire their party, your win is almost a guarantee.
Some worlds exclusively mention in their mission that only their party can be allowed to take it. They even pay extra to the mercenary halls to present their missions to the party first.

Their party is one of the few parties that the mercenary halls approach on their own and offer money to take missions from their halls. Just having the Leander Family step into a mercenary hall pretty much changes its fate.
Even the other mercenary parties have become wary of them to the point where they do not take any missions that put them in the Leander Family’s opposition."
"I do not blame them. We saw it with our own eyes, didn’t we? Ransa was completely helpless against them. The world that resisted our forces for thousands of years crumbled within two days."

On the other side, as the women returned to Core, Nux appeared in front of them and greeted them with a smile,
"You are getting more and more popular."
Ember smiled at those words. She was happy.
After a long time, she felt… useful.
To command millions of soldiers… it felt exhilarating. Especially when her Law connected every single one of those soldiers and boosted their and her strength.
The Goddess of War.
This is what the people call her now, and she couldn’t help but smile at that name every time it was mentioned.
"Look at you smiling like that, oh mighty Goddess of War~"
Astaria chuckled as she stared at her sister. The rest of the women all had teasing smiles on their faces.
The Goddess of War lowered her head, embarrassed.
"Gosh, I want those people to see her right now."
Allura chuckled.
"They probably wouldn’t believe it."
Thyra shook her head.
"Mhm, they would think it’s a clone that is being used to ’defile the image’ of their Goddess."
Aisha added dramatically, and the rest of the women laughed.
"Alright, girls, stop teasing my Goddess."
Nux jumped in as he gently hugged the War Goddess. Ember, using this opportunity, quickly wrapped herself around Nux.

It was her reward for bringing another victory and, most importantly, information about a few other worlds Nux could target. As their influence grew, so did their information network. It had become much easier for them to find things out.
So much so that by now, Nux had already devoured twelve worlds, and the universe was losing its mind.
Nux smiled as he saw Ember act like that. Then, his eyes fell on Vulpiana and,
"Your mother has summoned you."
"What?"
Vulpiana was taken aback.
"Your mother. She says she needs to see you."
"Why?"
"How am I supposed to know what the Dawnshade Leader is thinking?"
Nux questioned back with a playful smile on his face.
Vulpiana just stared at this man in silence.
Then, she just sighed.
"Open the portal."
She requested.
Nux nodded, and the portal to Yrniel was opened.
"I’ll be back soon."
"Looks like you do not wish to stay away from me. Look how unwilling you seem even when your mother called for you."
Nux teased. Vulpiana, however, shook her head as she walked into the portal with her face flushed.
Nux chuckled when he saw that. Then, he closed the portal.
"That woman is annoying,"
Aisha complained again.
"But she is quite useful,"
Ember added, and as Nux turned towards the War Goddess, she continued,
"Yes, I admit that we are quite limited whenever we are around her since we need to make sure we do not reveal something important, but at the same time, I cannot disregard her ability.
She is strong."
"I agree,"
Thyra nodded as well.
As an assassin, she could tell just how useful the Fox’s ability was. And of course, Nux knew that as well.

After all, she managed to trick even him using her ability. Not many could boast of doing the same, especially when they were at the same cultivation level as him. The only reason he was even able to react in time properly was because Aeliana had pushed him to the point where his Zenith Flow was working again.
If it wasn’t for that, then… even he would have lost that little bout between the two of them.
"Anyways, why do you think Faelara called her?"
Suddenly, Astaria questioned as she turned towards Nux.
Nux, however, shook his head,
"I really do not know."
But then, a screen appeared in front of him, and in that screen, Vulpiana’s vision was shown.
"But I guess we will find out soon enough,"
Nux spoke with a smile, and the others widened their eyes in surprise.
"Nux, when did you…"
"What? Did you think I wouldn’t learn from my stalker teacher?"
Nux laughed as he glanced at Aeliana, who looked away, as if this wasn’t related to her at all.

chapters.title: Chapter 1871: Young Lady, you did what!?
paragraphs: "You wished to see me, Mother?"
Vulpiana questioned as she glanced at the woman standing in front of her.
Right now, they were in a sealed space where no one could keep an eye on them. For someone like Faelara, this was nothing more than a parlor trick.
"You broke through, huh…"
Faelara’s eyes shined as she stared at her daughter.
Vulpiana smiled, and unable to control herself anymore, Faelara pulled her daughter into her embrace and patted her back.
"You did well…"
She spoke, her tone unusually gentle.
A small smile appeared on Vulpiana’s face. No matter what, her mother’s embrace was still the most comforting spot in the Universe.
Vulpiana hugged her mother back, and an extreme sense of comfort washed over her.
Everything she had been through all this time, everything that exhausted her, it all went away.
"Look at you~"
Faelara chuckled.
"You just got stronger, then why are you acting weak?"
The mother Fox questioned with a light smile.
The daughter, however, just buried her face into her mother’s breasts and,
"I am still weak."
"You are much stronger than you think, my Vul."
Faelara spoke as she ruffled Vulpiana’s hair.

"I think I should go out more often, else the people would forget I even exist."

"So? Why couldn’t I contact you?"
Faelara questioned directly.
"I wasn’t in Yrniel."
Faelara raised her eyebrow.
"You should be in a separate dimension that is connected to Yrniel, no? The Artifact shouldn’t be restricted by those dimensions."

"I was not."
Vulpiana shook her head.
"I participated in the War."
"The War…?"
"There is an ongoing War between two High-Level Worlds."
Vulpiana informed.
"You participated in that…?"
Faelara blinked in surprise and stared at her daughter.
"We participated as mercenaries. We were only dealing with Low-Level Worlds."
"Only?"
Faelara raised her eyebrow.
Those were some arrogant words, especially since they came from a girl who herself came from a Low-Level World.
"This is what I wish to talk to you about."
Vulpiana spoke with a solemn look on her face as she stared at the woman in front of her.

"What is it?"
She questioned.
"They are strong."
Vulpiana spoke.

"Those women, they are much stronger than what we assumed.
When I say we ’only’ dealt with Low-Level Worlds, I was acting arrogantly.
That is what those worlds are to them, ’only’ Low-Level Worlds."
Vulpiana stared, and Faelara’s expression changed.
"When those women fight, Sovereigns do not stand a chance. Mother, they can change the entire flow of the War to their side and win with minimal casualties.
The Outer Space knows them as the Leander Family, and in all the Wars they have participated in till now, they haven’t lost a single one."
"Not a single one…?"
Faelara couldn’t believe what she was hearing.
"Not a single one."
Vulpiana nodded, and she wasn’t done yet.
"And this is when not all of them participate in the War.

"What about him?"

"He doesn’t participate either."

"But I am certain of it, Mother,
He is much stronger than any one of them.

"What makes you sure?"

"Mother."
"Hmm?"
"For me, you were always the strongest Divine there was. I couldn’t even imagine the possibility of any other Divine Stage Cultivator being able to defeat you."

"But even you couldn’t do what he did."
"What did he d—"

It was Vulpiana.
"He was able to sense it and react to it before I could get close to him."
"H-How did yo—"

"The second time, he didn’t even allow me to get close."
Vulpiana’s voice echoed throughout the surroundings.
And suddenly, another Vulpiana stepped out right in front of Faelara, and as she stared at her mother, she spoke with a solemn look on her face.
"Actually, he was able to find my real location and even managed to pull me out. I was completely helpless against him, Mother.
And I have never felt such a way ever since I became a Divine Stage Cultivator. Even when I faced the Primordials of those worlds, I wasn’t scared since even they couldn’t find my real body.
They could never truly kill me.
No one could ever truly kill me.
But he can…"
Vulpiana spoke, and hearing those words, Faelara just stared at her daughter in disbelief.
"Wait, wait, wait, wait,
What do you mean ’even when you faced Primordials of those worlds!?’
Young Lady, you did what!?"

chapters.title: Chapter 1872: You are being summoned to Sylveris…
paragraphs: "Wait, wait, wait, wait,
What do you mean ’even when you faced Primordials of those worlds!?’
Young Lady, you did what!?"
Faelara shouted as she stared at her daughter in anger and disbelief.
The ’Young Lady’ had said too many absurd things at the same time, Faelara needed to take it slow.
"Mother, we participated in wars of low-level worlds. Obviously, there were Primordials there. All low-level worlds have Primordials."
Vulpiana spoke as if it was obvious.
"That, I understand, but what do you mean when you say you were facing Primordials!? Are you telling me you were fighting Primordial-level beings!?"
Faelara didn’t even consider the possibility of how impossible that was. She was too worried about her daughter to think about it.
Vulpiana, however, had already expected such a reaction and replied calmly.
"She was with us."
"Who?"
"The Ancestral Order’s Leader, Aeliana Ruinous."
"She was with you…?"
Faelara’s eyes widened in disbelief.
Vulpiana nodded.
"Every time a Primordial tried to attack us, she appeared and…"
The fox daughter lowered her head as she recalled that sight.
"Every time she appears, she gets rid of all enemy Primordials on her own, ending the war once and for all…"
"This…"
Faelara stood still, not knowing how to react.
"Mother, that woman is extremely strong. Even Primordials are utterly helpless around her."
Vulpiana spoke with a solemn look on her face, and as she heard her words, Faelara’s expression changed yet again.
"What are you trying to get at, Vul?"
She questioned directly.
"I am saying that we were wrong."
Faelara stared at her daughter, and Vulpiana continued,
"Every single one of them is ridiculously strong, and if all of them come together to protect Yrniel,
Then there aren’t many threats that could actually harm Yrniel, especially when we still do not know about the ’secret weapon.’
Mother,
We should have sided with Yrniel."
Vulpiana spoke, and Faelara just turned silent.
Did she not know this before?
Of course, she did.
The very fact that Yrniel survived even after all these worlds were after it was enough to prove its strength.
But…
Was there anything she could do in this situation…?
There was not…
After all…
"Vul…"
Faelara called out, staring at her daughter with moist eyes.
"I am so sorry about this…"
Seeing that expression on her mother’s face, Vulpiana’s expression changed as she quickly rushed towards her.
"Mother, what happened!?"
Faelara stared at her daughter and,
"You are being summoned to Sylveris…"
"What…?"
Vulpiana’s expression changed.
Sylveris was the first world the Fox Ancestors contacted the moment they came to Yrniel. The world where it all began.
A world… the foxes went to when they were ’Marked.’
"Did they find out…?"
Vulpiana questioned as she narrowed her eyes.
She was only supposed to go to Sylveris when she became a ’Saint Stage Cultivator.’ Of course, in Sylveris’s eyes, she was still a Semi-Saint…
Not to mention that she was supposed to be on a mission as a ’Spy’ to gather information.
For them to call her like this…
"They found out that the Mana Apocalypse had ended, so when they asked about you, I told them you were on the mission, but they want you to continue your mission after being marked."
Faelara answered with a solemn look on her face.
Inwardly, however, her heart was breaking into pieces.
After all, what mother would want to send her daughter, knowing that she would be turned into a slave?
But once again, Faelara was helpless.
If she tried to resist, she, together with her people, would all perish.
After all, those beings held that much power over them.
Vulpiana turned silent.
Faelara’s body continued to tremble, cursing her weakness as she stared at her daughter.
This was the only thing she wanted to avoid. She did everything in her power. She even sent her daughter away to that man in order to avoid this, but…
In the end, she failed…
And now, her daughter would need to pay for her weakness.
Seeing her mother acting so weakly, Vulpiana felt a lump in her throat, her heart felt heavy.
She moved forward as she hugged her mother and patted her back.
"Everything will be alright, Mother. I assure you."
She spoke with a determined look on her face.
Faelara, on the other hand, could only hug her daughter weakly.
"When do I leave…?"
Vulpiana questioned.
Faelara stayed silent.
"Mother?"
Vulpiana called out, and with a heavy heart, Faelara answered,
"Right now.
They want me to send you there the moment you get here."
Vulpiana nodded.
She already knew that some of the Foxkins must have already reported her arrival to Sylveris. If she didn’t get there soon enough, her mother and her people would be the ones to suffer.
"Please send me, Mother."
Vulpiana spoke with a solemn look on her face.
Faelara glanced at her daughter one last time, then she nodded, sending her daughter into the lion’s den with her own hands.
The Fox Leader activated her Law, and a white light enveloped Vulpiana’s body before she disappeared, leaving only Faelara inside the room.
Vulpiana, who appeared in an entirely new world, looked around and quickly realized that she was in some hall.
She wanted to look around and assess her surroundings a bit more, but—
"You are here."
She heard a hoarse voice.
She looked ahead, and her eyes fell on a being with a thin, green, crystallized body and purple eyes.
*Picture*
Usually, Vulpiana would have been surprised by his appearance. However, after seeing everything she had seen, she was getting numb to it.
"A Sovereign? I was told you were a Protector."
The being frowned.
"I chanced a few encounters in my mission."
"Encounters that turned you into a Sovereign? I didn’t have those encounters when I was a Protector."
Clearly, the being was suspicious. However, seeing that Vulpiana was silent, he just shrugged and—
Your next journey awaits at freewebnovel
"Are you prepared to be marked?"
He questioned as he walked toward Vulpiana.
The Fox didn’t move and continued to stare at the being in front of her. Seeing that, he chuckled,
"You are like your mother.
Unnecessarily big attitude as if you own the world, but in the end, here you are, leaving your life in another being’s hands."
As he mocked the Fox, he placed his index finger on her forehead.
Vulpiana sensed a foreign energy entering her body. However, before she could even understand what it was, the energy disappeared, seeping deep into her body.
"You can leave."
The being dismissed her with a bored look on his face.
Vulpiana blinked in surprise. She didn’t think she was summoned here just for this.
The being, however, simply walked away without explaining anything, and suddenly, a white light surrounded Vulpiana’s body, and she disappeared again.
She had returned to Yrniel.
"M-Mother…?"
She was a little taken aback.
"They keep the meetings short to make sure they are not traced back. Even Yrniel’s Will won’t notice that you were gone."
"How is that possible?"
Vulpiana frowned.

"Because you were not sent to a dimension connected to Yrniel. It was that being’s projection that you saw. Of course, since it was merely a projection, incapable of doing anything, Yrniel wouldn’t be able to detect it.
This is how these people have been avoiding Yrniel and the Order all this while."
Faelara explained, and Vulpiana nodded in understanding.
Back in Sylveris, as the being disconnected himself from his projection, he returned to his room.
However, the moment he walked in—
He froze as he saw a human sitting in front of him with a casual smirk on his face.

What surprised the being even more wasn’t the fact that this man was able to sneak into his room. It was that this being, who was clearly a foreign entity, was able to enter Sylveris, and Sylveris’s Will didn’t warn him about him.
"Who ar—"
Before the being could say anything—
"You know…"
The human called out.
Then, he stared at him with his golden eyes and—
"I do not like when people touch what I desire.
Even if it was just your projection, and what you ’touched’ was merely a clone, I still do not like it."
"A clone…?"
The being narrowed his eyes.
"Ah, right,
You failed to notice, didn’t you?
Well, that girl is quite capable. I agree."
The man nodded at his own words. Then, he stared at the being and—
"Not to mention, you are retarded, fucking Ben 10 alien freak."
"Wh—"
Before the being could say anything, Nux disappeared and…
The being’s nightmare began.

chapters.title: Chapter 1873: I have ways to get the answers I need
paragraphs: "You bastard! Who are you!? Identify yourself!"
One of Sylveris’s Primordials, who had ’marked’ Vulpiana, Aghaast, shouted in anger as he glared at Nux, who had pushed him into a portal that took him to an entirely different world.
At first, Aghaast was intimidated. After all, this man had managed to sneak into his room. What’s worse? Sylveris’s Will didn’t warn him about him.
This man had the ability to trick a World’s Will.
Obviously, Aghaast would be intimidated. However, the instant he was pushed into the portal and sensed the quality of this man’s energy, he understood something.
This man…
He was a Sovereign.
A mere Sovereign… had dared to act like this in front of him…
Aghaast was filled with fury.
Embarrassment, that is what he felt.
And now, he was going to wash away this embarrassment with his own hands.
"I will ask you one last time.
Are you a Human from Yrniel? How did you know the coordinates to our world? Did those Foxes needlessly open their mouths?"
He asked a few questions. However, seeing how this human only stared at him with a curious look on his face, without answering any of his questions, Aghaast’s anger rose even further.
That look…
It felt like this human was looking at him as if he was some sort of toy…
It was extremely degrading and disrespectful.
Aghaast decided it.

He clenched his fist, and soon, he raised his eyebrow.
"This thing is stronger than I thought."
The human commented, somewhat amazed.
Aghaast, on the other hand, was surprised. A Sovereign was able to block his attack… and to think he was able to do it with such ease.
’Do Humans normally have such reflexes? Or has he trained in a certain manner?’
Soon, Aghaast came to a conclusion.
’He must have low strength since he focused so much on his speed and agility.’
With that, the plan changed.

Nux chuckled as he stared at the cheap copy in front of him.

"Alright, Ben 10, you had your fun.
Now it’s my turn."

"H-How… you are a S-Sover—"

His Soul was pushed out of his body.

"W-What is this!? What did you do!?"
His soul screamed.
Nux, on the other hand, took out a familiar needle and stared at the Soul in front of him.
"I have a few questions I need answers to."
Nux smiled and then,
"And coincidentally, just like you,
I have ways to get the answers I need, ways you will not like, Sylverisian."
Repeating the similar words, Nux walked towards Aghaast’s soul that was desperately trying to get away and injected the needle into his forehead.
"AAAGGGGGGHHHHHHHH!!!"
The Primordial’s scream echoed throughout the new Dead World Nux had found just to deal with troublesome matters like these.
"Try and hold on to your sanity.
I still need answers."
Nux suggested generously.

chapters.title: Chapter 1874: Two Factions
paragraphs: "Is it alright to kidnap a World Leader like this?"
Felberta, who walked out of Nux’s shadow and hugged him from behind, questioned.
Feeling the familiar warmth and those ample breasts his head was buried into, a satisfied smile appeared on Nux’s face as he closed his eyes.
The Eldraeth Progenitor smiled as she sensed Nux’s emotions. Her hands gently held Nux’s before she tightened her hug around him, burying the man into her body.
For a moment, Nux didn’t say anything. He just enjoyed his first wife’s warmth. Then, to answer her question, he finally opened his mouth.
"It will be fine."
"Won’t they notice if he is gone for too long?"
Felberta questioned.
"If he was anyone else, they probably wouldn’t have noticed, but he is a World Leader, one of the strongest there. They would notice his missing presence very quickly."
"Of course they will."
Nux nodded.
Then, he just shrugged,
"But because he is a World Leader, they wouldn’t think too deeply. After all, what World Leader gets kidnapped from his own world without being able to alert anyone else?"
He laughed.
Then, he rubbed Felberta’s palm with his fingers and,

"The people rely too much on the World’s Will. The World Leaders are used to it. They are too comfortable thinking no one can enter their world without alerting them, and they are right to think that since, theoretically, this isn’t possible.
But…"
"But it is different when it comes to the Anomaly."
Felberta chuckled.
"Well, yeah."
Nux shrugged.

"Since the other World Leaders didn’t sense anything out of the ordinary, they would simply assume that he had gone somewhere on his own accord. Funnily enough, rather than worrying about him, they would get wary of him.
Where did he go?
Why do we not know anything about it?
Who did he meet?
Is it an ally? Or an enemy?𝕗𝕣𝐞𝐞𝘄𝐞𝚋𝚗𝗼𝘃𝗲𝗹.𝚌𝕠𝚖
All these questions would get in their heads, and it will cause a rift between the leaders instead."
Nux chuckled, finding all this amusing.
Felberta smiled as well. Her eyes fell on Aghaast, and seeing his soulless body lying on the floor while his soul hovered in the air, not reacting to anything around it anymore,
Yes, it was yet another one of the broken souls that fell victim to the cruel Soul Severance.
"Anyways, what should we do about him now?"
At Felberta’s question, Nux finally decided to move out of the heaven he was buried in and stared at the being in front of him.
Then, with a wave of his hand, he placed Aghaast’s soul back into his body, and his purple eyes, which had dimmed down, came back to life again.
The being, however, just like others, didn’t react.
Nux then placed his hand on his head and,
"Don’t resist."
He ordered as his energy entered the being’s body. Strange patterns started appearing on his body as he read Aghaast’s memories. Once he was done, a frown appeared on his face.
For now, however, he decided not to think about it. He opened a portal and carried Aghaast into his room again.
Then, using his ability, he manipulated his memories to forget everything that happened from the point he met him and returned back to Felberta, closing the portal.
"He will find out, you know."
Felberta commented.
Memory erasing was effective, but beings at Primordial levels would be able to sense the ’blanks’ in their minds and piece it together.
"I didn’t erase his memory."
Nux shook his head.
"What?"
Felberta frowned.
"I manipulated it according to his habits."
Nux shrugged.
"By the time he realizes something is wrong, he will have other things to worry about."
He spoke, his mind forming a devious plan.
And Felberta, who could read his emotions, couldn’t help but be curious.
"What did you see in his memories? Did you get information regarding the Foxes?"
Nux nodded.
"How’s the situation? Who are we up against?"
The Eldraeth questioned directly.
After all, she already knew what Nux was thinking. She knew what he was going to do, and since he had already decided, it was obvious that she and the others would be there right next to him as well.
"Have you ever wondered that if even the lowest level worlds are part of factions and are somehow connected to the Supreme Worlds, why is Yrniel different?"
Nux questioned back.
"Isn’t that because we are too far away from the Supreme Worlds?"
"That is correct."
Nux nodded.
"But this doesn’t mean that we do not have our own problems to deal with.
Since the Supreme Worlds’ influence doesn’t spread to this area, the worlds here have created their own independent factions, and currently,
There are two major factions here."
"Don’t tell me…" Experience tales with freewebnovel
Felberta’s expression changed.
"Yep, the one who is after the Foxes is one of these two factions."
Felberta turned silent.
"Just like Faelara told me before, these people are actually after Yrniel’s ’Secret Weapon,’ and they are using the Foxes to learn more about it.
The faction wants to get their hands on this weapon and get rid of the enemy faction."
"How do they know if this ’secret weapon’ is strong enough?"
"It is because when Yrniel was attacked before, one of the strongest experts of this faction was sent to lead the charge,
But it only awakened that monster from his sleep…"
Nux answered, and Felberta didn’t need to think about what happened next.
"They were wiped out, huh?"
Nux shrugged.
"The faction never tried to directly get involved with Yrniel again and decided to use the Foxes. But well…
They didn’t really succeed, and now, it seems like they are losing patience."
"How strong is this faction?"
Felberta questioned with a curious look on her face.
"They have five Middle Level Worlds at the top. The rest are low-level worlds we don’t have to consider."
"Five Middle Level Worlds…"
Felberta muttered, and Nux nodded with a solemn look on his face.
"They are a problem.
There’s a total of eighteen Transcendents in the faction. We stand no chance in a direct confrontation."
"Then… are we going to abandon the Foxes?"
Felberta questioned.
She knew Nux would do that if he had to choose.
Nux, however, shook his head and smiled mischievously.
"I said we stand no chance in a direct confrontation.
Who said we are going to do that?
It is time to use our long-time enemy to our advantage."
Nux’s grin widened.
